Made by D.P.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Crawford D.S.

Stepan Ivanovitch FEDOROFF, was born on August 28,
1920 in Vladivostok, Maritime Province. His late father,
a Chinese, was engaged in commercial business in that city.
The applicant arrived in Shanghai together with his mother
in 1926. From 1927 to 1929 he attended the Russian
Commercial School. Upon the death of his mother in 1929
he was placed by the French Consular Authorities in the
St. Francis Xavier's College in which he studied up to
October, 1938.

The applicant is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
concerning him.

日期：1938年12月12日。

主题：S. I. Fedoroff，申请加入上海义勇军（S.V.C.）俄罗斯团。

由副巡官 Pavloff 撰写，由 C. Crawford 助理总监转呈。

Stepan Ivanovitch FEDOROFF，于1920年8月28日出生于滨海省符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）。其已故父亲为华人，在该市从事商业活动。申请人于1926年与其母一同抵达上海。1927年至1929年，他就读于俄罗斯商业学校。1929年其母去世后，他被法国领事当局安置于圣方济各沙勿略学院（St. Francis Xavier's College），并在此就读至1938年10月。

申请人已在莫尔缅路（Moulmein Road）118/1号的俄罗斯侨民委员会登记。

工部局警务处档案中无关于他的记录。

（印：MUNICIPAL ... 12.12.38）

D. P. S. Pavloff

H.B.M. Consul-General in Vladivostok. In 1924 , the applicant
was unofficially adopted by Mr. and Mrs. Hill and has
since been known under the name of Hill. He arrived in
Harbin from Vladivostok in 1927 together with Mr. and Mrs.
Hill and resided there until 1929 when he left Harbin
for England , where until 1933 he attended the St. Georges
School on the Isle of Wight. He arrived in Shanghai in
1933. In the beginning of 1935 he entered the Public and
Thomas Hanbury School , graduating from same in 1937.
In June 1938 he obtained his present position with Alexander
Clark Co. , ( Shanghai ) Ltd.
Mr. G.C. Hill died in Shanghai in 1938 and at present
the applicant is residing together with Mrs. Hill at 331
Route Bourgeat.
The applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee , 118/1 Moulmein Road.
There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to his character.

Alexeye Prokopievitch ANNENKOFF（即 HILL），俄国人，于1916年3月29日出生于西伯利亚克拉斯诺亚尔斯克。其姑母 E. Bouonoff 嫁给了 G.C. Hill 先生，后者曾任英国驻符拉迪沃斯托克总领事。1924年，申请人被 Hill 夫妇非正式收养，此后即以 Hill 为名。1927年，他随 Hill 夫妇从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达哈尔滨，并居住至1929年，随后离开哈尔滨前往英国，在怀特岛（Isle of Wight）的圣乔治学校（St. Georges School）就读至1933年。他于1933年抵达上海。1935年初，他进入汉璧礼西童公学（Public and Thomas Hanbury School），并于1937年毕业。1938年6月，他在亚历山大·克拉克公司（Alexander Clark Co., (Shanghai) Ltd.）获得现任职位。
G.C. Hill 先生于1938年在上海去世，目前申请人与 Hill 夫人同住于蒲石路（Route Bourgeat）331号。

Semen Nikolaevitch NIKOLAEFF, Russian, was born
on September 1, 1912 in Simbirsk Province, Russia. From
1918 to 1927 he resided together with his parents on the
Saghalin Island. In 1927, he proceeded to Harbin and until
1931 worked there as a bus conductor and subsequently as a
bus driver. He arrived in Shanghai in June 1931 and soon
afterwards obtained a position as a chauffeur with Mr. M.
Artischeff, proprietor of a dairy farm in the French Con-
cession. On March 14, 1932, he joined the Russian Regiment,
S.V.C. in which he served until October 31, 1937, when he
resigned on his own accord. Upon leaving the Regiment, he
worked casually as a driver and for the past six months was
employed by the City Express Transportation Company, 613/55
Avenue Joffre.

The applicant is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to his character.

Made by D.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Gaetani

1. Ivan Ivanovitch SAHNO, Russian, was born on June 17,
1913 in Harbin, Manchuria. He first came to Shanghai in 1934
and, according to his own statement, lived here for a period
being unemployed and supported by his father. On February 2,
1935 he joined the Auxiliary Detachment of the French Police
in which he served until 8-5-35 when he deserted in order to
proceed to Harbin. He returned to Shanghai in April, 1938 and
worked casually until September of the same year when he was
engaged by Calatroni, Hsieh & Co., as a godown keeper. He
left that employment on his own accord recently in order to
join the Russian Regiment.

The applicant's mother and brother left Harbin for
the U.S.S.R. in 1936. His sister at present is residing in
Harbin.

On his first arrival in Shanghai he registered with
the Council of United Russian Organizations ( SORO ) but at
present is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Committee,
118/1 Moulmein Road.
（左侧印章及手写字：MUNICIPALITY 9-1-39）

2. Georgy Makarovitch BAKLANOFF, Russian, was born on
May 15, 1902, in Barnaul, Siberia. He is reported to have
escaped from the U.S.S.R. to Manchuria in 1931 and subsequently
resided in Harbin. He arrived in Shanghai in the s.s.
"Tsingtao Maru" on December 7, 1938. He is registered with
the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road on the
strength of passport No. 10844 issued by the Harbin Police on
1-8-38.

Being a new arrival in Shanghai, the applicant is not
known in the local Russian community.

1. Ivan Ivanovitch SAHNO，俄国人，于1913年6月17日出生于满洲哈尔滨。他于1934年首次来到上海，据其自称，在此期间失业，由其父亲供养。1935年2月2日，他加入法国警察辅助队，服役至1935年5月8日，当时他为了前往哈尔滨而擅离职守。他于1938年4月返回上海，打零工直至同年9月，随后被 Calatroni, Hsieh & Co. 雇佣为仓库管理员。最近他自愿辞去该职，以便加入俄罗斯团。

申请人的母亲和兄弟于1936年离开哈尔滨前往苏联。其姐妹目前居住在哈尔滨。

他初抵上海时在俄罗斯联合组织理事会（SORO）登记，但目前已在莫尔缅路（Moulmein Road）118/1号的俄罗斯侨民委员会登记。
（左侧印章及手写字：MUNICIPALITY 9-1-39）

2. Georgy Makarovitch BAKLANOFF，俄国人，于1902年5月15日出生于西伯利亚巴尔瑙尔。据报道，他于1931年从苏联逃往满洲，随后居住在哈尔滨。他于1938年12月7日乘坐“青岛丸”号（Tsingtao Maru）轮船抵达上海。他凭哈尔滨警方于1938年8月1日签发的第10844号护照，在莫尔缅路（Moulmein Road）118/1号的俄罗斯侨民委员会登记。

作为新近抵沪者，申请人在当地俄罗斯社区中不为人知。

and holds passport No.99, issued on 24-5-38, by the

Nikolai Michailovitch SOGRIN, Russian, was born on
April 20, 1907 in Perm Province, Russia. He is reported
to have left Russia, together with his two brothers in 1920
and subsequently resided in Harbin. Upon graduating from a
local high school and the school of accountancy he was
employed by Vorontzeff Bros. and Co. as a bookkeeper at
their oil factory at Hailar Station, Chinese Eastern Railway,
from April 1926 to October 1927, after which he worked as a
lumber contractor of the Chinese Eastern Railway up to 1930.
In the beginning of 1931, he proceeded to Tsingtao where he
was employed as a manager and representative of Vorontzeff
Bros. & Co. After liquidation of the branch office of the
above company in that city, he proceeded to Shanghai arriving
here in September 1933. Here he worked casually until March
1934 when he was engaged by the China General Omnibus Company
as a ticket inspector. Leaving this position on his own
accord in September 1937 he secured an employment with A.A.
Meyer and was placed in charge of their chartered lighters
at Hunt's Wharf. At present he is employed by the same
company as a bookkeeper at their general office, 97 Yuen
Ming Yuen Road.

The applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, and with the Police Bureau of
the City Government of Shanghai (Reg. Cert. no. 13348 issued
on 8-9-37).

While in Shanghai, he did not come to the notice of the
Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an
undesirable nature.

制作人 D.S. Pavloff 转呈人 G Crawford

尼古拉·米哈伊洛维奇·索格林（Nikolai Michailovitch SOGRIN），俄国人，1907年4月20日出生于俄罗斯彼尔姆省。据报他于1920年与两个兄弟离开俄罗斯，随后居住在哈尔滨。从当地高中及会计学校毕业后，他于1926年4月至1927年10月受雇于沃龙采夫兄弟公司（Vorontzeff Bros. and Co.），在中东铁路海拉尔站的该厂油厂担任簿记员，此后直至1930年，他作为中东铁路的木材承包商工作。1931年初，他前往青岛，在那里受雇为沃龙采夫兄弟公司的经理及代表。在该市上述公司分行清算后，他前往上海，于1933年9月抵达此地。在此他打零工直至1934年3月，当时他被中国公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Company）聘为查票员。1937年9月他自愿离职，随后在A.A. Meyer公司找到工作，负责该公司在亨特码头（Hunt's Wharf）的包租驳船。目前，他在同一家公司位于圆明园路97号的总办事处担任簿记员。

申请人已在莫利爱路118/1号的俄国侨民委员会登记，并在上海市政府警察局登记（登记证号13348，签发于1937年9月8日）。

在上海期间，他未因任何不良性质的活动引起工部局警务处的注意。
（批：抄送上海义勇队特别官员档案）
（批：A.G. Farley）

1. Sergey Arsentiévitch SOROCHINSKY, Russian, was
born on March 23, 1905, at Bouhedu Station, Chinese Eastern
Railway. Upon graduating from a local primary school he worked
as a chauffeur for various periods in Harbin, Hailar and
other railway stations on the Chinese Eastern Railway until
May 1938 when he proceeded to Tientsin, where, according to
his own statement, he worked in the same capacity until
September of the same year when he left for Shanghai. Here
on September 25, 1938 he joined the Auxiliary Detachment
of the French Police, from which he resigned on his own
accord on 28-12-38. Being a new arrival in Shanghai he is
little known locally.

2. Dionisy Yakovlevitch CHELPANOFF, Russian, was born
on March 10, 1906 in Tomsk Province, Siberia. He is reported
to have escaped from the U.S.S.R. to Manchuria in 1930 and
subsequently worked in the Railway Police at Eshaho Station,
Chinese Eastern Railway. In September 1938 he proceeded
to Tientsin and there joined the Railway Guards and was
stationed at a coal mine, situated between Tsinanfu and
Tsingtao. In December 1938 he was arrested for
insubordination and after being kept prisoner for 17 days
at the so called "White House" in Tientsin, he was deported
to Shanghai, arriving here on 8-1-39.

He holds passport No.1928 issued on 27-9-38 by
the Police Bureau of the Greater Tientsin.

3. Alexey Sergeyevitch KOOLINBERG, Russian, was born
on May 15, 1919 at Petrograd, Russia, He is reported to
have left Russia together with his parents in 1921 and
subsequently resided in Harbin. In 1934 he left Harbin for

2. 迪奥尼西·雅科夫列维奇·切尔帕诺夫（Dionisy Yakovlevitch CHELPANOFF），俄国人，1906年3月10日出生于西伯利亚托木斯克省。据报他于1930年从苏联逃往满洲，随后在中东铁路额绍站（Eshaho Station）的铁路警察部门工作。1938年9月，他前往天津，并在那里加入铁路护卫队，被派驻在济南府和青岛之间的一处煤矿。1938年12月，他因不服从命令被捕，在天津所谓的“白房子”被囚禁17天后，被驱逐至上海，于1939年1月8日抵达此地。

December 14, 1920 in Kamchatka Region, Siberia. He is
reported to have escaped from the U.S.S.R. to Manchuria
together with his parents in 1930 and subsequently
resided in Harbin until 1933 when he proceeded to Shanghai.
Here he entered the Ecole Remi, in which he studied up
to 1935. In the end of the same year he was engaged
as a messenger by W. Futterer, 1201-1203 Bubbling Well Rd.
He worked with this firm, first as a messenger and later
as a shop assistant, until 21.1.39 when he resigned on
his own accord.

2. Boris Vladimirovitch GVOZDOFF, Russian, was born
on May 24, 1920 at Nikolsk-Ussuryish, Maritime Province,
Siberia. He is reported to have left Russia together
with his parents in 1922 and for the following five years
resided in Tientsin after which he left for Harbin.
On November 11, 1938 he arrived in Shanghai and on November
26, of the same year joined the Auxiliary Detachment
of the French Police, in which he served until 18.1.39
when he resigned on his own accord.

FILE

March 25, 1921 at Echo Station, Chinese Eastern Railway.
He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on 12.1.39, travelling
on passport no. 3186 issued on 30.8.38 by the Harbin
Police.

Being a new arrival in Shanghai he is not known
locally.

1. Peter Georgievitch AMBARIANTZ, Russian of
Armenian origin, was born on July 2, 1920 at Chan-
Chun, Manchuria. He arrived in Shanghai in the
beginning of 1932 and soon afterwards entered the
St. Francis Xavier's College, which he attended up
to 1934. From 1934 to 1937 he studied at the
Anglo-French College, Range Road. Upon leaving the
latter college he worked for a short period in the

an active part in the crime and that it was his

Applicant's brother, S.G. Ambariantz, is

He is reported to have arrived in Harbin in 1919
and to have resided in that city until his departure
to Shanghai. He arrived here on 29-1-39, travelling
on passport No. 20877 issued on 8-12-38 by the
Harbin Police.
His brother N.F. Zabal is at present serving

Georgy Andreyevitch BELKIN, Russian, was born
on April 27, 1898 in Transbaikal Province, Siberia.
He is reported to have left Russia in 1920 and
subsequently resided in Hailar, Manchuria, until
the outbreak of the Sino-Russian hostilities in 1929,
after which he proceeded to Mukden. According to his
own statement, while in Hailar he operated a photo-
studio and later worked in the same capacity in Mukden.
He arrived in Shanghai from Mukden in April 1931 and
soon afterwards opened a photo-studio at 728 Avenue
Joffre, which was later removed, first to 1205 Bubbling
Well Road in 1934 and then (in 1935) to 999 Avenue
Joffre. At present he is a staff photographer of the
newspaper "Evening Echo" and also works independently
as a photographer at his home, 1003/2 Avenue Joffre.
The applicant is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.
While in Shanghai, he did not come to the notice
of the Municipal Police in connection with any
activities of an undesirable nature.

FILE
Maximilian Nikolai Victor ZALEVSKY, was born
on December 12, 1918 at Vladivostok, Siberia. He is
reported to have left Vladivostok for Manchuria together
with his parents in 1922 and to have subsequently
resided in Harbin until 1923 when he proceeded to
Shanghai. Here in 1924 he entered the Shanghai American
School in which he studied up to 1933. Later he
attended the Gonzaga College, graduating from same in
1937. In August 1937 he obtained employment with the
"Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury" and worked in that
concern until September 1938. In October of the same
year he secured his present position as a manager of
the Shipping Department of the Shotter, Madar and Co.,
225-6 Sassoon House.
The applicant claims to be a Pole by birth,
however, he is registered with the Police Bureau of the
City Government of Shanghai as a Russian Emigrant.
(Reg. Cert. No. 22092 issued on 2-6-37).
Applicant's father, who until recently lived
separately from his family, came to the notice of the
Municipal Police in November 1931, when a complaint was
made at the Wayside Police Station by one Ling Ching
Keoung, Zalevsky's former partner in the Wine Factory
on East Seward Road, accusing Zalevsky of having
misappropriated the sum of 9,000.00 dollars. However,
as the case was of a purely civil nature, no police
action was taken in connection with the matter.

Maximilian Nikolai Victor ZALEVSKY，1918年12月12日出生于西伯利亚符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）。据报他于1922年随父母离开符拉迪沃斯托克前往满洲，随后在哈尔滨居住，直至1923年动身前往上海。1924年，他进入上海美国学校（Shanghai American School），就读至1933年。后来他就读于贡萨加学院（Gonzaga College），并于1937年毕业。1937年8月，他在《上海晚邮与信使报》（"Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury"）获得职位，并在该机构工作至1938年9月。同年10月，他获得了目前在肖特·马达尔公司（Shotter, Madar and Co.，地址：沙逊大厦225-6号）航运部经理的职位。
申请人声称出生时为波兰人，然而，他在上海市政府警察局登记为俄国侨民。（登记证号 22092，签发于1937年6月2日）。
申请人的父亲此前与家人分居，于1931年11月引起工部局警务处注意，当时一名叫 Ling Ching Keoung（音译）的人在路边巡捕房提出投诉，指控 Zalevsky 挪用款项9,000.00美元。Ling Ching Keoung 是 Zalevsky 在前东熙华德路（East Seward Road）酒厂的 former partner。然而，由于该案纯属民事性质，警方未就此事项采取任何行动。

（印：REPORT CONFIDENTIAL）
Subject A.N. Cherniavsky , application for enrolment in the Transport Company
S. V. C.
Made by D. S. Pavloff. Forwarded by C. Crawford S. J.

Alexander Nikolaevitch CHERNIAVSKY , Russian , was
born on September 6 , 1910 in Kuban Province , Russia. He is
reported to have left Russia in 1918 and to have subsequently
resided in Harbin until 1927 , after which he came to
Shanghai. From 1927 to 1932 he failed to find permanent
employment but worked in casual jobs:- one time as an interior
decorator , later as a reporter of the Russian daily newspaper
" Slovo " and he is also reported to have served in the
Russian Detachment of the S.V.C. from 10-5-30 to 10-6-30.
He left Shanghai for Canton in 1932 and after a short
stay there , during which , according to his own statement ,
he was employed by the Shameen Police , returned to Shanghai.
Upon his return here he was engaged by the S.S. Shoe Store ,
199 Nanking Road as a shop assistant . Later he worked in
the same capacity with the Shanghai Shoe Manufacturing Com-
pany , 21 Boone Road. From 1935 up to the present moment he
has been unemployed and at present resides together with his
mother , proprietrix of a boarding house , at 1315 Yu Yuen
Road.
On March 6 , 1931 , the applicant was fined $30.00 by
the 1st. S.S.D. Court on a charge of Assault with Intent to
Cause Bodily Harm. ( S. W. F.I.R. 185/31. )

Copy to S. O. S. V. C.

（印：机密报告）
事由 A.N. Cherniavsky，申请加入上海义勇队（S.V.C.）运输连
由 D. S. Pavloff 呈报。经 C. Crawford S. J. 转递。

Alexander Nikolaevitch CHERNIAVSKY，俄国人，
于 1910 年 9 月 6 日出生于俄罗斯库班省。据报他于
1918 年离开俄罗斯，随后在哈尔滨居住至 1927 年，之后
来到上海。从 1927 年至 1932 年，他未能找到固定
工作，但从事过零工：一度担任室内装潢师，后来担任
俄文日报《言论报》（"Slovo"）的记者，另据报他曾
于 1930 年 5 月 10 日至 1930 年 6 月 10 日期间在上海
义勇队俄国分队服役。
他于 1932 年离开上海前往广州，在那里短暂停留
期间，据其自称受雇于沙面警察，之后返回上海。
回到上海后，他被南京路 199 号的 S.S. 鞋店聘为
店员。后来他在同一家公司——布恩路 21 号的上海制鞋
公司——担任同样的职务。从 1935 年至今，他一直失业，
目前与其母亲（一家寄宿公寓的业主）共同居住在愚园路
1315 号。
1931 年 3 月 6 日，申请人因犯有意图造成身体伤害
的袭击罪，被第一特区地方法院罚款 30.00 元。（S. W. F.I.R. 185/31。）

抄送上海义勇队参谋长。
（印：归档） D. S. Pavloff
D. S.
副总监（特科 A 组）致 副总监（特科）
3 月 7 日

Subject I.A. Mishin, applicant for enrolment in No. 3 (Vol) Company,
S.V.C.
Made by. D.S. Pavloff, Forwarded by. C. Crawford. D.S.

Igor Alexeyevitch MISHIN, Russian, was born
on February 19, 1911 at Moscow, Russia. He is
reported to have left Russia in 1922 together with
his parents and to have subsequently resided in
Harbin until 1933, after which he came to Shanghai.
After a short stay in this city he proceeded to
Kulin and resided there until 1934, when he returned
to Shanghai. In the beginning of 1935 he left
Shanghai for Hankow.

On August 28, 1938 he and four other Russians
were arrested by the Chinese Authorities in Hankow.
They were kept prisoners for six days after which
they were released and advised to leave Hankow within
14 days. The applicant left Hankow on 17-9-38 and
travelled to Shanghai via Hong Kong, arriving here
on 5-10-38.

On February 11, 1939 he secured his present
employment, as a supervisor with Fagan & Co., 281
Kiangse Road.

The applicant is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road, on the
strength of passport No. 827 issued on 12-9-38 by
the Hankow Police.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
concerning this person.

由 D.S. Pavloff 呈报，经 C. Crawford. D.S. 转递。

Igor Alexeyevitch MISHIN，俄国人，于
1911 年 2 月 19 日出生于俄罗斯莫斯科。据报他于
1922 年随父母离开俄罗斯，随后在哈尔滨居住至
1933 年，之后来到上海。在本市短暂停留后，他前
往桂林（Kulin），并在那里居住至 1934 年，随后返回
上海。1935 年初，他离开上海前往汉口。

1938 年 8 月 28 日，他和另外四名俄国人
在汉口被中国当局逮捕。他们被囚禁了六天，之后
获释，并被要求在 14 天内离开汉口。申请人于
1938 年 9 月 17 日离开汉口，经香港前往上海，于
1938 年 10 月 5 日抵达此地。

1939 年 2 月 11 日，他获得了目前的职位，
担任江西路 281 号 Fagan & Co. 公司的监工。

申请人凭汉口警察机关于 1938 年 9 月 12 日签
发的第 827 号护照，在莫利哀路 118/1 号俄国侨民
委员会登记。

工部局警务处档案中无关于此人的记录。

副总监（特科）。

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY No. 917/236 Date March 8, 1939）
Subject A.V. Igoshin, I.A. Mescheriakoff and G.A. Markevitch, applicants
for enlistment in the Russian Regiment. S.V.C.
Made by D.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Gasford. S.I.

(1) Alexander Vladimirovitch IGOSHIN, Russian,
was born on October 19, 1921 in Harbin, Manchuria.
He arrived in Shanghai in December 1932 and soon after-
wards entered the Commercial School of the Russian
Orthodox Confraternity in which he studied until 1937.
On December 8, 1937 he joined the Auxiliary Detachment
of the French Police in which he served until 15-6-38,
when he resigned on his own accord. Since then he has
been unemployed.

(2) Igor Alexandrovitch LESCHERIAKOFF, Russian,
was born on January 4, 1921 in Harbin, Manchuria. He
arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on February 25, 1939
and resided together with Dr. G.K. Krivoroochko, at 651,
Weihaiwei Road, Apt. B.02.

(3) Georgy Alexandrovitch MARKEVITCH, Russian,
was born on June 14, 1921 in Nikolsèvsk-on-Amur, Siberia.
He is reported to have escaped from the U.S.S.R. to
Manchuria, together with his mother in 1929 and to have
subsequently resided in Harbin. He arrived in Shanghai
in 1932 and during the same year entered the Ecole Remi
in which he studied up to 1938.

All applicants are registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
concerning any of the above persons.

Copies to Major Banks. Murphy.
FILE J.B. (批：2 a Pavloff-)

Subject (in full) G. Serejnikoff, applicant for enrolment in the Signals Company,
S. V. C.
Made by D.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Crawford. S.I.

Georgy Nikolaevitch SEREJNIKOFF, Russian, was
born on November 26, 1917 at Astrakhan, Russia. He
arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostok in 1922 together with
his parents. In 1929 he entered the First Russian
School (now A.S. Poushkin Memorial School), graduating
from same in 1937. During the same year he entered the
Aurora University, in which he studied up to December
1938. In January 1939 he was engaged by the Shanghai
Power Company as an apprentice in their chemical
department.

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to his character.

D.C. (Special Branch)

I. Victor Alexandrovitch TIHONOFF , Russian , was
born on May 28 , 1920 at Handaochedze Station , Chinese
Eastern Railway. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin
on March 11 , 1939 and is not known locally.

2. Yury Alexandrovitch BELIAKOFF , Russian , was
born on October 26 , 1920 in Harbin , Manchuria.
He arrived in Shanghai in May 1936 and during the
same month entered the First Russian School ( now
A.S. Poushkin Memorial School ) . Having graduated
from same in 1937 , he has since been studying in
the Centre Technique Superieue , 200 Route Remi.

（印：MUNICIPAL SPECIAL 21.3.39）

3. Boris Alexyevitch KOROSTELOFF , Russian , was
born on December 10 , 1920 in Harbin , Manchuria.
He arrived in Shanghai in 1928 and in 1931 entered
the Commercial School of the Russian Orthodox
Confraternity , in which he studied up to 1933.
Upon leaving the school he was unemployed.

All three applicants are registered with the
Russian Migrants' Committee , 110/1 Moulmein Road.
There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records concerning them.

Subject. A.A. Rozenberg , applicant for enlistment in No. 3 ( Volunteer )
Company , S. V. C.
Made by D. S. Pavloff. Forwarded by C. Crawford
Alexander Alfredovitch ROZENBERG , Russian ,
was born on November 2 , 1910 in Harbin , Manchuria.
Upon graduating from a local high school in 1930
he entered the 2nd. Harbin School of Dentistry ,
graduating from same in 1933. He arrived in Shang-
hai in the beginning of 1934 and in September of
the same year was engaged by L.M. Gorovitz , Dental
Surgeon , 97 Route Vallon , as an assistant dentist.
In August 1938 he left that place of employment
on his own accord and proceeded to Harbin. He
returned to Shanghai in December of the same year
and on 19-12-38 secured his present position as
a dentist with M. Klatchko , Dental Surgeon , 26
The Bund.
While in Shanghai , the applicant did not
come to the notice of the Municipal Police in
connection with any activities of an undesirable
nature.

Russian Regiment , S. V. C.
Made by D. S. Pavloff. Forwarded by C. [Signature] S. I.

I. Andrey Ivanovitch LOOSHNIKOFF , Russian , was
born on August 28 , 1918 in Viatka Province , Russia.
He is reported to have left Russia in 1922 together
with his parents and to have subsequently resided
in Harbin , where for the past two years he served
in the Harbin Railway Police. He arrived in Shang-
hai on March 21 , 1939 and is not known locally.

2. Anatoly Emelianovitch BELOFF , Russian , was
born on August 10 , 1918 in Harbin , Manchuria.
After graduating from a local middle school he ,
for the past two years , served in the Harbin Rail-
way Police. He arrived in Shanghai on March 14 ,
1939 and resided at 314/3 Hardoon Road , together
with his brother-in-law , I.T. Aksenoff , Sergeant
of the Shanghai Municipal Police.

The above two applicants are registered
with the Russian Emigrants' Committee , 118/1
Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records concerning them.

enlistment in the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.
Made by D.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Crawford. J!
1. Tadeosh Genrichovitch ELOVITSKY, Russian,
was born on March 27, 1903 in Vladivostok, Maritime
Province, Russia. He is reported to have left
Russia in 1921 and to have subsequently resided in
Harbin. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in July
1929 and on August 1, 1929 joined the Russian Regi-
ment, S. V. C. He served in the Regiment until
September 1, 1934, when he resigned on his own accord.
During the same month he joined the Auxiliary
Detachment of the French Police in which he served
until 16-8-35 when he was dismissed for borrowing
money from a money lender. He worked casually un-
til May 1937 when he proceeded to Hankow, where he
resided until April 11, 1939, after which he re-
turned to Shanghai.
2. Georgy Ivanovitch YUMSHANOFF, Russian, was
born on November 28, 1916 at Station Bukhedu,
Chinese Eastern Railway. According to his own
statement, he attended a Russian School in Harbin
from 1928 to 1933 after which he resided at Station
Bukhedu together with his parents for a period.
Some time towards the end of 1934 he proceeded to
Mukden where he was employed with Liddell Bros. &
Co., Ltd. until August, 1937. He is reported to
have arrived in Shanghai from Dairen in February,
1938. Since his arrival until January 1939 he
was employed as a mechanic with the Far Eastern
Salvage Association, 2 French Bund.

1. Tadeosh Genrichovitch ELOVITSKY，俄国人，
1903年3月27日出生于俄罗斯滨海省符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）。
据报他于1921年离开俄罗斯，随后定居哈尔滨。
他于1929年7月从哈尔滨抵达上海，并于1929年8月1日加入上海义勇队（S.V.C.）俄国团。
他在该团服役至1934年9月1日，当时他自愿辞职。
同月，他加入法国警察辅助分队，服役至1935年8月16日，因向放债人借款而被解雇。
此后他打零工直至1937年5月，随后前往汉口，在那里居住至1939年4月11日，之后返回上海。
2. Georgy Ivanovitch YUMSHANOFF，俄国人，
1916年11月28日出生于中东铁路布赫杜站（Station Bukhedu）。
据其自称，他于1928年至1933年在哈尔滨的一所俄国学校就读，
之后与父母在布赫杜站居住了一段时间。
1934年底左右，他前往沈阳，在 Liddell Bros. & Co., Ltd. 工作至1937年8月。
据报他于1938年2月从大连抵达上海。
自抵达后至1939年1月，他受雇于法外滩2号的远东打捞协会（Far Eastern Salvage Association），担任机械师。

Subject F.F. Lange, applicant for enlistment in the Russian Regiment,
S.V.C.
Made by D.S. Pavloff. Forwarded by C. Crawford J.D.

Fedor Feodorovitch LANGS, Russian, was born
on May 11, 1907, in Omsk, Siberia. He is reported
to have left Russia in 1920 and to have subsequently
resided in Harbin until 1922, after which he
proceeded to Shanghai. He served in the Russian
Regiment, S.V.C. for the following periods:-
1-6-28 to 1-11-28 and from 1-10-30 to 6-3-32,
leaving the Regiment on his own accord on both
occasions. Between July 7, 1932 and May 10, 1933
he worked as a foreman at the French Tramway
Company's depot. Leaving that company on his own
accord, he worked casually until June 1935 when he
was engaged as a foreman welder by the Shanghai
Dockyard Ltd. On November 5, 1937 his services were
dispensed with owing to a reduction in staff.
From July 15, 1938 to April 12, 1939 he served as
an anti-piracy guard with the China Navigation
Steamship Company.

The applicant is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

On September 28, 1933 he was sentenced by the
1st Shanghai Special District Court to 12 days'
imprisonment on a charge of Negligent Driving and
Breach of Traffic Regulation No. 34.

Made by. D.S. Pavloff Forwarded by. [Signature] 8. 8.

Pavel Vassilievitch BELOVCHIKOFF, Russian,
was born on July 12, 1921 in Harbin, Manchuria. He
arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in 1927 together with
his parents and resided here until 1936 after which
he proceeded to Tientsin together with his father.
He returned to Shanghai in May 1938 and in September
of the same year was engaged as a bar boy by the
Bee-Ba-Bo Cabaret, 1337 Yu Yuen Road. He left that
place of employment in January, 1939 and from last
worked as a delivery boy with the Alliance Bakery,
58-60 Route Pere Robert. He discontinued his work
on or about 25th of this month.

References obtained from Mr. A. Irshenko,
proprietor of the Alliance Bakery and Mr. V. Ivanchenko,
proprietor of the Bee-Ba-Bo Cabaret, are not in the
applicant's favour. They describe him as an
irresponsible youth of lazy habits, lacking education
and discipline.

His father, who it is believed is in Tientsin
at present, forms the subject of Criminal record,
No.F1209, the particulars of which are as follows:

2nd S.S.D. Court. Trespassing Acquitted 24.4.29

1st S.S.D. Court. False Pretences Not guilty. 25.10.32
(Verdict brought in as the complainant refused
to attend court)

2nd S.S.D. Court. Receiving morphine injection. 1 year & 6 months imprisonment. 5.3.36

Alexander Petrovitch DROSDOFF, Russian, was
born on December 24, 1917 at Harbin, Manchuria. He
arrived in Shanghai in 1924 together with his sister
Miss N.P. Drosdoff. In 1930 he entered the Public
and Thomas Hanbury School, graduating from same in
1935. In June 1936 he was engaged by I. Shickman,
Fur & Skin Dealer, and proceeded to Tsinang and later
to Tientsin, where he worked in the head office of
the above concern. He left that place of employment
on his own accord in June 1938 and returned to
Shanghai. In November of the same year he secured
his present employment as a chief clerk with the
Globe Wireless, Ltd., 51 Canton Road.

The applicant has four sisters, two of whom
are reported to be in Hongkong at present and the
other two reside in Shanghai.

Since 1930 the applicant is reported to have
resided together with Mr. A.M. d'Eca, Portuguese,
who, it is believed, intends to adopt the applicant
in the near future.

He is not registered with the Russian Emigrants
Committee or with any other Russian public association
and is not in possession of any document of identity.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records concerning the applicant.

Subject A.E. Fester and A.P. Shavikin, applicants for enlistment in the

Made by D.S. Pavloff. Forwarded by C. Crawford J.J.

Anatoly Edwardovitch FESTER, Russian,
was born on December 29, 1920, at Spassk, Maritime
Province, Russia. He is reported to have escaped
from the U.S.S.R. together with his parents in
1928 and to have subsequently resided in Pogranichnaya
Station, Chinese Eastern Railway. He arrived in
Shanghai in 1930 and in the beginning of 1931
entered the Ecole Remi. Upon leaving the
school in 1936 he assisted his father who at that
time was the owner of Fester Sausage Factory, 76c
Route Vallon. This factory closed down in June
1937 owing to business depression and since then up to
May 1938 the applicant was employed with Lang &
Semin Sausage Factory, 28 Route Dolfus. He left
that place of employment on his own accords and
from July 1938 to January 1939 worked with Saratov
Sausage Factory, 126-128 Route Dufour.

The applicant is registered with the
Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records detrimental to his character.

Alexander Pavlovitch SHAVIKIN, Russian,
was born on February 12, 1921 at Tientsin. He
first arrived in Shanghai together with his parents
during the same year and resided in this city until
1924 after which the family proceeded to Manila, P.I.
Returning to Shanghai in 1927 he attended the Ecole
Remi from 1930 to 1935.

Foreign Affairs Section June 27, 19
Foreign Affairs Section June 27, 1946

SUBJECT:- Soviet-Russian Residents of Wayside -
Proposed Establishment of Club.

According to local Soviet press reports, Soviet-
Russian residents of Wayside district propose to open in
the near future their own small club. For this purpose
an initiative group headed by V.V.JOUKOFF, V.KUDIN and
B. MOCHALOFF, having permission from Chairman of the Coun-
cil of the Soviet Citizens' Society, rented the ground floor
of premises No. 163 Chaoufeong Road comprised of several
rooms. Repair work is in progress in the premises in
question.

The aims of the new club include the organisation
of a reading room, library, chess circle. Lectures, conferen-
ces, parties, dancing and other forms of entertainment and
recreation can be held in the club.

In its work the initiative group is glad to have
full assistance of the newly formed Society of Soviet Re-
sidence. Registration of prospective members is being
carried daily from 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. at the above address
and when a sufficient number of members have been register-
ed, elections of the club's committee will be held.

A. Prokofiev

Officer 1/e Foreign Affairs,
Section.

外事科 1946年6月27日

主题：- 韦斯特区（Wayside）的苏俄居民 -
拟建立俱乐部。

据当地苏联媒体报道，韦斯特区（Wayside district）的苏俄居民提议在不久的将来开设他们自己的小型俱乐部。为此，一个由V.V. JOUKOFF、V. KUDIN和B. MOCHALOFF领导的发起小组，在获得苏联公民社会理事会主席的许可后，租下了兆丰路163号 premises 的一楼，包括几个房间。相关场所的修缮工作正在进行中。

新俱乐部的目标包括设立阅览室、图书馆和国际象棋小组。俱乐部内可举办讲座、会议、聚会、舞会及其他形式的娱乐和休闲活动。

发起小组很高兴得到新成立的苏俄居民协会（Society of Soviet Residence）的全力协助。 prospective 成员的登记工作每天下午7点至9点在上述地址进行，当登记成员达到足够数量时，将举行俱乐部委员会的选举。

A. 普罗科菲耶夫

外事科

Julian Lucianovich KOSHMANN, Russian, born

Isaac Solomonovich MILLER, Russian of Jewish origin, born on December 13, 1921 at Harbin. He is reported to have arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in 1929 together with his parents. Here he attended the Shanghai Jewish School until 1936, after which he studied in the Lester School of Technical Education for about six months (in 1937) and in the Public & Thos. Hanbury School from January to May, 1938. In May, 1938 he was engaged by the Shanghai Telephone Company as an apprentice and is still working in this capacity.

He resides at 5 Yang Terrace, Weihaiwei Road, together with his parents, Mr. & Mrs S.B.F. Miller and his four brothers. The father and two elder sons are connected with Miller's Transport Co., 106 Peking Road. Two brothers of the applicant, A.S. Miller and D.S. Miller, are reported to be employed with the China General Omnibus Co., as mechanics and are members of the Transport Company, S.V.C.

Applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants Committee, Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records concerning this person.

Mihail Iakovlevich VOLKOFF, Russian, born on
May 21, 1907 at Shuanchenpo Station, Chinese Eastern Rail-
way. According to his own statement, he attended a pri-
mary school until 1921, after which he studied in a tech-
nical school attached to the Central Workshops of the Chi-
nese Eastern Railway, Harbin. In 1923 he proceeded to the
U.S.S.R. where he joined the army. In 1924 he fled back to
Manchuria. For the following 14 years he resided in va-
rious places of the Chinese Eastern Railway Zone being en-
gaged mainly in hunting and collecting material for vari-
ous zoological museums etc. and now describes himself as
a taxidermist.

He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in June, 1938
and has since been residing in this city, assisting in
business his brother, V.Ya Volkoff, who is the proprietor
of Arana Co., 90 Rue Tenant de la Tour, ( X-ray & Electro-
medical Appar. Manufacturers).

He is registered with the Russian Emigrants' Com-
mittee, Moulmein Road, on the strength of Certificate of Re-
sidence No.4595 issued on 12-4-38 at Harbin. At present he
resides at 66/48 Route Lorton.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
concerning this individual.

米哈伊尔·雅科夫列维奇·沃尔科夫（Mihail Iakovlevich VOLKOFF），俄国人，1907年5月21日出生于中东铁路双城堡站。据其自述，他就读小学至1921年，随后在中东铁路哈尔滨中央工厂附属技术学校学习。1923年他前往苏联并参军。1924年他逃回满洲。在此后的14年间，他居住在中东铁路沿线各地，主要从事狩猎以及为各类动物学博物馆等收集标本的工作，目前自称是标本剥制师。

served in the ranks of the White army during the civil
war in Siberia in 1918 - 1920. In 1921 he arrived in

employed for various periods by different firms and also

Here he worked as a journalist in the Russian newspaper
"New Trail" for about ten months (in 1936) and in the
"Novosti Dnia" (in 1937), after which he left for
Tientsin where from May to November, 1937 he was
employed with the General Export Company. Returning to
Shanghai in November, 1937 he worked as a private teacher
for a short period, then as a translator in the newspaper
"Slovo" for four months and from September, 1938 has
been working as a journalist in the "Novosti Dnia".

In 1930 while in Harbin he became a naturalized
Chinese citizen. However, he is registered with the
Russian Emigrants Committee, Moulmein Road, and with the
French Police as a Russian emigrant on account of the
fact that he has no Chinese passport. He states that
recently he applied to the Chungking Government for a

Arcady Alexeyevitch MIHAILOFF-MITCHELL,

Vladivostok. In September of the same year he entered
the Thomas Hanbury School for Boys and graduated from
same in December 1926. Then he worked casually until
September 1930 when he obtained a position as a
supervisor with the China Printing & Finishing Company
Ltd. at one of their mills in Pootung. In February

April of the same year secured a position as a meter
inspector with the French Tramway & Electric Company.

owing to a reduction in staff. From September 1937

Studio, 104 Bubbling Well Road.

Made by D.S. Pavloff    Forwarded by C. Crawford O.J.

1.    Vassily Iosifovitch PAVLOFF, Russian, was
born on March 20, 1917 in Transbaikal Province,
Russia. He is reported to have left Russia together
with his parents in 1919 and to have subsequently
resided in Harbin, Manchuria. In August 1934 he
arrived in Shanghai from Harbin and in October of
the same year joined the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.
In April 1939 he left the Regiment of his own accord
and in May of the same year joined the Auxiliary
Detachment, French Police. On June 26, 1939 he
resigned from the Detachment on the excuse that he
wanted to proceed to Harbin.

      There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records concerning this applicant.

2.    Uriy Alexandrovitch BELELIUBSKY, Russian, was
born on April 11, 1910 in Riazan Province, Russia.
According to his own statement, he left Russia
together with his parents in 1920 and subsequently
resided in Harbin, Manchuria. In July 1932 he
arrived in Shanghai from Harbin and in August of the
same year joined the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.
On October 31, 1937 he left the Regiment of his
own accord. Soon afterwards he obtained a position
as a chauffeur with Harden & Co. and later worked
in the same capacity with the British Transportation
Company, 299 Kiukiang Road.

Anatoly Leontievitch OKBAKOVSKY, Russian, was
born on July 30, 1908 in Chernigoff Province, Russia.
He is reported to have left Russia together with
his parents in 1917 and to have subsequently resided
in Harbin, Manchuria. In October 1936 he arrived in
Shanghai from Harbin. In January 1937 he and another
Russian, M. Ilvis, established their own business
under the style Universal Advertising Company, 309
Route Cardinal Mercier. In June of the same year
he suspended conducting the business owing to the
lack of funds and proceeded to Tientsin. In June
1938 he returned to Shanghai and on August 9, 1938
was engaged as a draughtsman by Moller & Company,
12 The Bund.

The applicant is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to his character.

after which he left for Mukden. He returned here in
March, 1939.

Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

Subject I.P. Rouchieff, V.S. Griakalo and P.K. Straut, applicants for
enlistment in the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.
Made by D.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C Crawford
1. Ivan Pavlovitch ROUCHIEFF, Russian, was born
on May 15, 1915, in Omsk Region, Siberia. According to
his own statement he left Russia together with his
parents in 1920 and subsequently resided in Harbin,
Manchuria. In September, 1933, he arrived in Shanghai.
On January 1, 1934, he joined the Russian Regiment,
S.V.C. On August 1, 1936, he left the Regiment of his
own accord. He worked casually until December 1937
when he joined the Auxiliary Detachment, French Police.
On April 14, 1938, he resigned from that Detachment.
Later he worked with the Campbell Paints Factory and
also with "Olma" Paints Factory. For the past six
months he was employed as a trainer with the Columbia
and Great Western Riding Academy.
2. Vladimir Sergeyevitch GRIAKALO, Russian, was born
on March 1, 1921, in Harbin, Manchuria. In September,
1933, he arrived in Shanghai and resided together with
Mr. Epifanoff, an employee of the Shanghai Water Works
Co., Ltd. In the beginning of 1934, he entered the St.
Francis Xavier's College and studied in it until 1939.
3. Pavel Karlovitch STRAUT, Russian of Latvian origin,
was born on May 20, 1914, in Harbin, Manchuria. From 1933
to 1935 he served as a Railway guard on the Mukden-Shanhai-
kuan Railway. From March 1935 to April 1939 he was
employed with the Political Section of the Police at
Manchouli and Harbin. On June 5, 1939, he, together
with several Japanese, left Harbin for Tientsin and later

Pavel Leopoldovitch AUMANN, Russian, was born
on June 29, 1916, in Habarovsk, Siberia. According
to his own statement, he left Russia together with
his parents in 1925 and subsequently resided in Harbin,
Manchuria. He first arrived in Shanghai on May 6, 1939,
and after a short stay in this city returned to Harbin.
On August 3, 1939, he returned to Shanghai and has since
been employed as a supervisor with H.B. Campbell, Oil
and Paints Factory, Route Tenant de la Tour.

Applicant's brother, E. Aumann, a musician by
occupation, has for the past three years been employed
with the Park Hotel orchestra.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
concerning this applicant.

1. Oleg Valentinovitch BRIZGIN, Russian, was born
on March 7, 1921, in Chefoo, China. From 1926 he
resided in Harbin, where in December 1938 he graduated
from a local high school.
He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on August
17, 1939, in the s.s. "Dairen" Maru.
Being a new arrival here, he is not known
locally.

2. Ivan Gavrilovitch STARIKOFF, Russian, was born
on April 25, 1906, in the Maritime Province, Russia.
He is reported to have left Russia in 1921 and to
have subsequently resided in Harbin until August
1933, afterwards coming to Shanghai.
On July 26, 1934, he was charged with Larceny
at the Shanghai Second Special District Court and
sentenced to 10 days' imprisonment. On September 13,
1934, he joined the Russian Regiment, S.V.C. and
served in it until April 12, 1938, when he resigned
of his own accord. Later he worked casually as a
chauffeur-mechanic and from September 1938 to August
1939 was employed in the same capacity with Mr. M.
Zeilig, 1248 Rue Lafayette, House 2.

3. Vasily Vasilievitch MAKEDONSKY, Russian, was
born on February 28, 1914, at the Boorea Station,
Amur Railway, Siberia. From 1922 to May 1934 he
resided in Harbin, after which he came to Shanghai.
On June 1, 1934, he joined the Russian Regiment,
S.V.C. He resigned from the Regiment of his own

4.  Nikolai Gernogenovitch BELOTZERKOVITZ, Russian,

    Province, Russia. According to his own statement,
    he left Russia together with his parents in 1924 and

5.  Igor Alexeyevitch STEPANOFF, Russian, was
    born on August 17, 1914, in Harbin, Manchuria.
    He first arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in 1930.
    During 1932 he served with the Russian Regiment,
    S.V.C. for two short periods, having been dismissed
    on both occasions. Later he proceeded to Tientsin
    and then Moukden where he was employed as a Railway
    Guard on Mukden-Kirin Railway. He reappeared in
    Shanghai in 1934, but having failed to secure any
    employment here, returned to Harbin after a short
    stay in this city.
        During his stay in Manchoukuo he worked as
    a chauffeur with Japanese military and private
    concerns in various cities of Manchoukuo including
    the Manchoukuo - U.S.S.R. border along Amur River.

2. Boris Trofimovitch FROLOFF, Russian, was born on October 1, 1917, at Veishahe Station, Chinese Eastern Railway. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on July 31, 1939 and resided together with his sister, Mrs. H. Opalinsky, 1222 Avenue Joffre.

Alexander Lvovitch CAPLAN , Russian Jew , was born
on April 13 , 1910 in Harbin , Manchuria. In 1914 he
arrived in Shanghai from Harbin together with his
parents. From 1915 to 1921 he attended the Thomas
Hanbury School , after which he entered the St. Francis
Xavier's College , graduating from same in 1926.
From 1927 to 1929 he was employed as a clerk with
the Shanghai Water Works Company , Ltd. Leaving that
company of his own accord he worked as a salesman with
the Office Appliance Company , Ltd. , for a period.
In November 1930 he secured a position as an assistant
manager with the Fox Films Corporation , 142 Nuseu Rd.
In March 1931 he was transferred to the Hongkong branch
of the same company. Returning to Shanghai in Janua -
ry 1933 he has since been employed as a general manager
with Warner Bros. First National Pictures Inc. , 142
Nuseu Road.
The applicant is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee , 110/1 Moukden Road .
There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to his character.

1. Boris Konstantinovitch PAHOMOFF, Russian, was
born on November 1, 1908, at Vladivostok, Maritime
Province, Russia. He is reported to have left
Russia in 1926 and to have subsequently resided in
Harbin, Manchuria. In 1927 he left Harbin for
Tientsin and in 1928 arrived in Shanghai from the
latter city. Here he worked casually until July,
1929 when he joined the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.,
on June 1, 1930, he left the Regiment of his own
accord. On January 1932 he obtained a position as
a chauffeur with the Asiatic Petroleum Co. (North
China) Ltd. Leaving that company of his own accord
in November 1935, he proceeded to Chefoo, where soon
afterwards he was engaged as a chauffeur by Mr. S. G.
Beare of H. B. M. Consulate-General. He returned to
Shanghai in June 1937 together with his employer and

I. Ilia Grigorievitch EFREMOFF, Russian, was born

arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostok in 1923 and resided
here until 1925 when he left Shanghai for Mukden where
he joined Marshal Chang Chung Chang's Army, leaving that
service in 1928, he returned to Shanghai. On April 16,
1929 he joined the Russian Regiment, S. V. C.. Leaving
the regiment of his own accord on August 1, 1929 he soon
afterwards obtained a position as a Police watchman with
Mr. F. A. Hsi, 153 Darroch Road. In August 1937 his
services were dispensed with following which he worked
casually until September 1, 1938 when he was engaged as
an Anti-Piracy Guard on the China Import and Export
Lumber Company's s.s. "Tsangtah". On April 30, 1939
his services were dispensed with and he has since been
unemployed.

2. Oleg Konstantinovitch ZNAMENSKY, Russian, was

11, 1934. On August 12, 1937 he joined the Auxiliary
Detachment, French Police, in which he served until
April 9, 1938 when he was dismissed for his wish to
resign before the expiration of his contract.

born on August 22, 1908 in Harbin, Manchuria. From 1926
to 1928 he served in Marshal Chang Chung Chang's Army
in Shantung and after the army had been disbanded, again
resided in Harbin until February 1930, after which he

1. Evgeny Vassilievich POGOODIN, Russian, was
born on November 24, 1914 at Krasnoyarak, Siberia. He
is reported to have left Russia together with his
parents in 1916 and to have subsequently resided in
Harbin, Manchuria. On June 23, 1938 he arrived in
Shanghai from Harbin and in September of the same year
joined the Auxiliary Detachment, French Police. On
February 9, 1939 he was dismissed from the Detachment
for being absent without leave.

Whilst in Harbin, the applicant became a Soviet
citizen, but prior to his departure to Shanghai he
applied for emigrant papers to the Bureau for the
Affairs of Russian Emigrants in Manchukuo and on 6-6-38
was issued by the latter institution with Provisional
Certificate No.304, which he still holds.

His father, Mr. V. Pogoodin, Russian emigrant,
is the proprietor of a licensed boarding house at 1166
Broadway East.

2. Anatoly Feofanovich MEDVIKUS, Russian, was
born on January 1, 1920 at Irkutsk, Siberia. From 1920
to 1929 he resided in Tientsin together with his parents.
He arrived in Shanghai from the latter city in 1929 and
in 1930 entered the Commercial School of the Russian
Orthodox Confraternity. In 1936 he left that school
and later studied in the First Russian School (now
A.S. Poushkin Memorial School) graduating from same in
1938. On August 1, 1938 he joined the Auxiliary

1. Levan Georgievich BARAMIDZE, Russian, was
born on October 24, 1917 at Harbin. He arrived in
Shanghai from Harbin on 1-4-38 and in May of the
same year secured employment as an assistant chemist
in the "Concordia Mineral Water Company", Avenue du
Roi Albert (now defunct). During July and August,
1939, he was employed as a ticket inspector with the
China General Omnibus Co. His brother is employed
with the service department of the X.M.H.A. Radio
Broadcasting Station, Race Course Road.

FILE
C

2. Constantin Ivanovich SHOOLGIN, Russian, born
on May 21, 1916 at Irkutsk, Siberia. According to his
own statement, he left Russia together with his parents
in 1921 and subsequently resided at Jalainor Chinese
Eastern Railway, where his father was employed as a
supervisor. The applicant arrived in Shanghai in July
1932 and soon afterwards obtained employment as an
assistant mechanic in the "Shelco", 958 Avenue Foch.
Leaving that place of employment of his own accord
some time towards the end of 1938, he was engaged in
January 1939 by the Press Wireless, 103 Kiukiang Road
as a mechanic. His services with this company were
dispensed with on 9-3-39 owing to a reduction in staff.

3. Georgy Ivanovich PROODNIKOFF, Russian, was
born on August 1, 1921 at Harbin. He arrived in
Shanghai from Harbin on September 25, 1939. One of his
cousins, named Grabovsky, is at present serving in the

Subject L.V. Fokin and A.M. Arshakuni, candidates for enrolment in the
Russian Regiment, S.V.C.
Made by D. S. Pavloff. Forwarded by C. Crawford.

1. Leonid Vassilievich FOKIN, Russian, was
born on July 2, 1916 at Cheremhovo, Irkutsk Province,
Siberia. He is reported to have left Russia for China
in 1920 and to have resided in Harbin together with
his parents until May, 1935 when he left for Shanghai.
On June of the same year he joined the Russian
Volunteer Company attached to the French Police, in
which he served until June 18, 1936 when he resigned
of his own accord. On November 16, 1936 he joined the
Russian Regiment, S.V.C. from which he resigned on
December 15, 1938. From 24-12-38 to 7-9-39 he was
employed as an Anti-Piracy Guard with Jardine Matheson
Co., Ltd. He resigned from this service of his own wish.
2. Andronik Nikitovich ARSHAKUNI, Russian of
Armenian origin, born on September 28, 1920 at
Blagoveschensk, Amur Province, Siberia. He is reported
to have left Russia together with his parents in 1921
and to have subsequently resided in Changchun and from
1924 - in Harbin. He first arrived in Shanghai in 1933
and until March 1938 attended the St. Francis Xavier's
College, after which he proceeded to Tsingtao. On
28-9-39 he returned to Shanghai.
Both Fokin and Arshakuni are registered with the
Russian Emigrants' Committee.
While in Shanghai they did not come to Police
notice.

（批：Copy to major Graham SVC）

D. C. (Special Branch).
D. S.

1. Leonid Vassilievich FOKIN，俄国人，1916年7月2日出生于西伯利亚伊尔库茨克省切列姆霍沃（Cheremhovo）。据报他于1920年离开俄国前往中国，并与父母一同居住在哈尔滨，直至1935年5月离开前往上海。同年6月，他加入附属于法租界公董局警务处的俄国志愿连，服役至1936年6月18日自愿辞职。1936年11月16日，他加入上海万国商团（S.V.C.）俄国队，并于1938年12月15日从中辞职。从1938年12月24日至1939年9月7日，他在怡和洋行有限公司担任防海盗警卫。他是自愿辞去该职务的。
2. Andronik Nikitovich ARSHAKUNI，亚美尼亚裔俄国人，1920年9月28日出生于西伯利亚阿穆尔省布拉戈维申斯克（Blagoveschensk）。据报他于1921年与父母一同离开俄国，随后居住在长春，自1924年起居住在哈尔滨。他于1933年首次抵达上海，并在圣方济各沙勿略学院就读至1938年3月，之后前往青岛。1939年9月28日，他返回上海。

Subject. I.I. Prosvirnin, candidate for enrolment in the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.

Made by. D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by. C Crawford. i J.

IGOR Ivanovich PROSVIRNIN ( or Prosvirnin-Platonoff ), Russian, born on November 7, 1921 at Harbin. He is reported to have arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in 1932 together with his parents. From 1933 to 1937 he attended the Commercial School of the Russian Orthodox Confraternity, following which he worked as an apprentice in Jenny's Motors, 177 Rue Amiral Courbet, for two months (in 1938) and later in the Victor's Vulcanizing Co., 396 Rue Bourgeat, for about six months. He left the latter company of his own accord in June, 1939. In September, 1939 he applied for enrolment in the Russian Auxiliary Detachment, French Police. His application was turned down as he is under the minimum age required by regulations of the Detachment ( 18 years ).

The applicant's brother, U.I. Prosvirnin-Platonoff is serving in the Auxiliary Detachment, French Police.

Their father, I.N. Prosvirnin-Platonoff, former employee of the Chinese Eastern Railway, has for the past six years been employed with the "Shanghai Laria" and resides at 166 Route Vallon. It appears that he was divorced from his wife in 1935 who at present is either married to or cohabiting with a certain American named McOrfney and resides at 836-C Cathay Flats, Avenue Joffre.

The applicant is registered with the Russian Emigrants Committee.

While in Shanghai he did not come to Police notice.

D.C. ( Special Branch )
G. Prokopov
J.U.I.

（左侧手写批注：Copy to Major G.ohan C）

IGOR Ivanovich PROSVIRNIN（或 Prosvirnin-Platonoff），俄国人，1921年11月7日出生于哈尔滨。据报他于1932年与父母一同从哈尔滨抵达上海。1933年至1937年，他就读于东正教兄弟会商业学校，随后在亚米拉·库尔贝路（Rue Amiral Courbet）177号的 Jenny's Motors 当了两个月学徒（1938年），后来又在布尔热路（Rue Bourgeat）396号的 Victor's Vulcanizing Co. 工作了约六个月。他于1939年6月自愿离开后者。1939年9月，他申请加入法租界警务处俄国辅助分队。因其年龄未达到该分队规章规定的最低年龄（18岁），其申请被驳回。

to have left Russia together with his parents in 1918
and to have subsequently resided in Manchuli for a
period and later in Harbin. In June 1939 he left Harbin
for Tientsin and on October 9, 1939 arrived in Shanghai
from the latter city in the s.s. "Hoten Maru".
Here he resided together with his sister at

he attended the Commercial School of the Russian

left that place of employment in July, 1938 and on

"Aramis", where, according to his own statement, he
secured a position with the Hongkong Dairy Farm. In
November of the same year his services were dispensed
with owing to a reduction in staff and he returned to
Shanghai on December 8, 1938. From January 1939 to
June 1939 he worked as an apprentice barber with the
Chernoff's Beauty Parlour, Route Say Zoong.

Made by D. S. Pavloff Forwarded by C. Gaford J D

Vladimir Victorovitch SHIROKOFF, Russian, was born on June 23, 1915 at Irkutsk, Siberia. According to his own statement, he left Russia together with his family in 1919 and for the following two years resided at Harbin. Later the family moved to Hankow. In 1926 the applicant came to Shanghai and until 1931 attended the St. Francis Xavier's College. During the same year his family consisting of mother and three sisters came to Shanghai from Hankow. For the following five years he resided together with them without fixed employment, being provided by his two elder sisters, who at that time were married to Mr. G.A. Warring, British, and Mr. L.A. Blackburn, British, respectively. In 1936, the applicant made a trip to Tientsin and in 1937 to Hankow, returning to Shanghai from the latter city in January, 1938. Still being supported by his sisters he did not bother himself with securing any employment except casual work until May, 1939, when he was engaged by the Globe Wireless Company, Ltd., 51, Canton Road. In July of the same year his services were dispensed with owing to his inefficiency and laziness.

At present he is still unemployed and resides together with his sisters, who conduct the "International Kitchen Bar", 7, Rue Chu Pao San.

He is in possession of passport No. 288, issued on September 11, 1937, by the Hankow Police.

（印：FILE C 1/1）

弗拉基米尔·维克托罗维奇·SHIROKOFF，俄国人，1915年6月23日出生于西伯利亚伊尔库茨克。据其自述，他于1919年随家人离开俄国，随后两年居住在哈尔滨。后来全家迁往汉口。1926年，申请人来到上海，并在圣方济各沙勿略学院（St. Francis Xavier's College）就读至1931年。同年，其由母亲和三个姐妹组成的家庭从汉口来到上海。在接下来的五年里，他与家人同住，没有固定职业，靠当时分别嫁给英国人G.A. Warring先生和英国人L.A. Blackburn先生的两个姐姐供养。1936年，申请人前往天津旅行，1937年前往汉口，并于1938年1月从后者城市返回上海。由于仍由姐姐们供养，除了做零工外，他并未费心寻找任何工作，直到1939年5月，他被广东路51号的环球无线电报有限公司（Globe Wireless Company, Ltd.）雇用。同年7月，因其效率低下和懒惰而被解雇。

目前他仍然失业，与经营朱葆三路（Rue Chu Pao San）7号“国际厨房酒吧”（International Kitchen Bar）的姐姐们住在一起。

他持有汉口警察局于1937年9月11日签发的第288号护照。

for enlistment in the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.
Made by D. S. Pavloff Forwarded by G. Crawford i. p.

（批：Copy to Major Graham L.V.C.）

1. Mihail Alexeyevitch CHOOIKOFF, Russian, was born on April 23, 1908 at Harbin, Manchuria. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in February 1934. Being a barber by occupation he worked in his professional capacity at various barber shops locally. In February 1938 he left Shanghai for Tsingtao, where according to his own statement he also worked in the same capacity. On October 6, 1939 he returned to Shanghai.

2. Boris Ivanovitch CHERNIH, Russian, was born on April 4, 1921 in Maritime Province, Russia. According to his own statement, he escaped from the U.S.S.R. in 1928 together with his sister and subsequently resided at Mukden. In 1931 he left Mukden for Tientsin where he entered the St. Louis College, graduating from same in 1938. He arrived in Shanghai on November 1, 1939 in the s.s. "Dairen Maru" and resided together with P.S. Madeyeff of the Shanghai Municipal Police.

3. Evgeny Ivanovitch GRISOFF, Russian, was born on November 20, 1920 at Nikolsk-Ussuriisk, Siberia. He is reported to have left Russia together with his parents in 1921 and to have subsequently resided at Harbin, Manchuria. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on October 29, 1939. Being a new arrival here he is little known in the local Russian community.

1. Mihail Alexeyevitch CHOOIKOFF，俄国人，1908年4月23日出生于满洲哈尔滨。他于1934年2月从哈尔滨抵达上海。作为一名理发师，他在本地各家理发店从事专业工作。1938年2月，他离开上海前往青岛，据其自述，他在那里也从事同样的工作。1939年10月6日，他返回上海。

2. Boris Ivanovitch CHERNIH，俄国人，1921年4月4日出生于俄国滨海省。据其自述，他于1928年与姐姐一起从苏联逃脱，随后居住在沈阳。1931年，他离开沈阳前往天津，进入圣路易斯学院（St. Louis College）就读，并于1938年毕业。他于1939年11月1日乘坐“大连丸”号轮船（s.s. "Dairen Maru"）抵达上海，并与上海公共租界工部局警务处的 P.S. Madeyeff 同住。

3. Evgeny Ivanovitch GRISOFF，俄国人，1920年11月20日出生于西伯利亚乌苏里斯克（Nikolsk-Ussuriisk）。据报道，他于1921年随父母离开俄国，随后居住在满洲哈尔滨。他于1939年10月29日从哈尔滨抵达上海。作为新来者，他在本地俄国社区中鲜为人知。

（批：Copy to major Graham SVC.）

1. Iosif Alexeyevitch ZAPOLSKY (ОГНЕФФ), Russian,
was born on September 9, 1921 at Vladivostok, Maritime
Province, Russia. He is reported to have left Russia
together with his parents in 1922 and to have
subsequently resided in Mukden.
His father, Mr. Ogneff, died in 1925 in Mukden,
and in 1926 his mother married one Mr. A. Zapolsky who,
it is said, officially adopted the applicant.
From 1935 the applicant resided at the St.
Tichon's Orphanage and from 1936 to 1939 attended the
First Russian High School (now A.S. Poushkin Memorial
School).

2. Mihail Victorovitch ZABOEFF, Russian, was
born on November 8, 1904 at Irkutsk, Siberia. According
to his own statement, he escaped from the U.S.S.R. to
Manchuria in 1927 and subsequently resided at Harbin,
where from 1929 to 1939 he was employed as a billiard
marker with the Hotel Modern Billiard Saloon. He
arrived in Shanghai in June 1939 and until present was
unemployed.

3. Pavel Ivanovitch CHESHKIN, Russian, was born
on May 31, 1908 in Maritime Province, Russia. He left
Russia in 1920 and resided at the Yaomin Station,
Chinese Eastern Railway for a period and later in
Harbin. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin in October,
1930. On May 28, 1931, he joined the Russian Regiment,

Made by D.S. Pavloff Forwarded by C.格拉森 30

(1) Alexander Maximovitch BOOBELOFF, Russian,
was born on December 12, 1917, at Harbin, Manchuria.
He first arrived in Shanghai in December, 1938, and
resided together with his aunt, Mrs. H.S. Babooshkin,
133 Route Vallon. In February 1939 he proceeded to
Harbin and in March of the same year returned to
Shanghai. In May 1939 he joined the Russian
Auxiliary Detachment of the French Police, but after
about one week's service received a telegram from
Harbin informing him of his father's illness, following
which he resigned and proceeded to Harbin. His
father, who was the chief of The Harbin Fire Brigade,
died on September 4, 1939. On October 29, 1939 the
applicant returned to Shanghai in the s.s. "Tsingtao
Maru".

（批：Copy to
Major Graham
SVC）

(2) Feodor Eremeyevitch BOLOTNENKO, Russian,
was born on September 16, 1918, in Maritime Province,
Russia. According to his own statement, he escaped
from the U.S.S.R. to Manchuria in 1932 and subsequently
resided in Harbin. He arrived in Shanghai from
Harbin on October 26, 1939 in the s.s. "Hoten Maru"
and is not known locally.

（印：FILE）

was born on January 1, 1921 at Tokyo, Japan. He
arrived in Shanghai from Korea together with his
mother in 1931 and resided here until 1933, after

Subject. B.N. Ivanoff and G.D. Ivanzoff, applicants for enlistment in the
Russian Regiment, S. V. C.
Made by. D. S. Pavloff Forwarded by. C. Graham. S.V.C.

Copy to Major
Graham, SVC

1. Boris Nikolaevitch IVANOFF, Russian, was
born on July 19, 1913 in Samara Province, Russia.
He is reported to have left Russia together with his
parents in 1919 and to have subsequently resided at
Manchouli Station, Chinese Eastern Railway until
1929 and later at Harbin. In May 1939 he left Harbin
for Dairen and on November 12, 1939 arrived in
Shanghai from the latter city.

2. Georgy Dmitrievitch IVANZOFF, Russian, was
born on August 30, 1921 at Harbin, Manchuria. He
arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on November 9, 1939
and resided at 162 C. Route Vallon, together with
his brother A.D. Ivanzoff, an employee of Bakerite
Company.

The above two applicants are registered with
the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to their characters.

D. S.

D. C.(Special Branch).

REPORT                       Date November 17, 1939.

Subject. L.V. Pioulsky and V.A. Velgous, applicants for enlistment in the
         Russian Regiment, S. V. C.

Made by. D. S. Pavloff        Forwarded by. C. Crawford

Copy to Major
Graham, S.V.C.

1. Lev Vladislavovitch PIOULSKY, Russian, was
born on October 25, 1905 at Mogilev, Russia. According
to his own statement, he left Russia in 1923 and
subsequently resided in Harbin. In 1925 he joined
Marshal Chang Chung Chang's Army in which he served
until 1927 when the army was disbanded. In 1927 he arrived
in Shanghai from Tsingtao and in March of the same
year joined the Russian Regiment, S.V.C. On March 31,
1929 he left the Regiment of his own accord and later
worked casually until March 1930 when he was engaged
as a chauffeur by Mr. B. Julien, proprietor of The
Pharmacie Generale, 949-951 Avenue Joffre. In November
1938 his services were dispensed with owing to Mr.
Julien's departure for France. In May 1939 the
applicant secured a position as an Anti-Piracy Guard
with Jardine, Matheson & Company, Ltd., but was
dismissed on November 3, 1939 for neglect of duty.

2. Victor Andreevitch VELGOUS, Russian, was born
on September 5, 1921 at Moscow. He is reported to have
escaped from the U.S.S.R. to Manchuria in 1928 together
with his mother and step-father, who is of the Chinese
nationality. The family proceeded to Chefoo where the
applicant resided until 1934 after which he came to
Shanghai. From 1934 to 1938 he studied in the First
Russian School (now A.S. Poushkin Memorial School) and
later attended the Pirogoff Memorial School, 249 Avenue
Haig. His mother and step-father, who are reported
to be unemployed at present, are residing at 697/1

Made by D. S. Pavloff. Forwarded by C. Crawford O. I

(copy to
Staff office
S.V.C.

Vladimir Andreyevitch ANTROPOFF, Russian, was born on April 23, 1919 at Moscow. He is reported to have left Russia together with his parents in 1922 and to have subsequently resided in Harbin. In 1926 he left Harbin for Tientsin where his father, a musician by occupation, was employed in his professional capacity. In 1930 the family proceeded to Java. In the beginning of 1931 they arrived in Shanghai. In 1933 the applicant entered the St. Francis Xavier's College graduating from same in 1936. During 1937 he studied in the Shanghai Business College, Arnhold Building, Szechuen Road. From November 1938 to April 1939 he attended the Radio Technical Centre, Avenue Haig, after which he secured his present employment as an office assistant with J. A. Thompson, Real Estate Agents, 57 Broadway.

His father is at present employed as a musician in the French Police Brass Band and also at the Weida Hotel, 993 Avenue Joffre.

While in Shanghai he did not come to the notice of the Municipal Police in connection with any activities of an undesirable nature.

D. S. Pavloff
D. S.

D. C. ( Special Branch ).

Vladimir Andreyevitch ANTROPOFF，俄国人，1919年4月23日出生于莫斯科。据报他于1922年随父母离开俄罗斯，随后居住在哈尔滨。1926年他离开哈尔滨前往天津，其父职业为音乐家，在当地从事专业工作。1930年全家前往爪哇。1931年初他们抵达上海。1933年申请人进入圣方济各沙勿略学院（St. Francis Xavier's College），并于1936年毕业。1937年间，他在四川路安诺大楼（Arnhold Building）的上海商学院学习。1938年11月至1939年4月，他在海格路无线电技术中心进修，此后在百老汇路57号房地产代理商 J. A. Thompson 处获得现任职位，担任办公室助理。

其父目前在法国警察局铜管乐队以及霞飞路993号伟达饭店（Weida Hotel）担任乐师。

在上海期间，他未因任何不良性质的活动引起工部局警务处的注意。

D. S. Pavloff
D. S.

D. C. （特务科）。

Mark Grigorievitch GECKER, Russian Jew,
was born on January 17, 1917 at Melitople, South
Russia. He is reported to have left Russia
with his parents in 1919 and to have subsequently
resided at Harbin. He arrived in Shanghai in
1924 and soon afterwards entered the Shanghai Jewish
School, graduating from same in 1936. In March
1938, he left Shanghai for Yokohama, Japan, where
he secured employment with Captain Vicary, Import
& Export. In December of the same year, he
left that place of employment of his own accord and
subsequently returned to Shanghai. From January
1939 till May of the same year, he was employed
with the Press Wireless Inc. 103, Kiukiang Road.
In September 1939 he secured his present position
with the China General Omnibus Co.

records detrimental to his character.

1. Uryi Alexandrovitch ESSINOFF, Russian,
was born on September 21, 1899 in Ekaterinoslav
Province, Russia. According to his own statement
he left Russia for China in 1920 and subsequently
resided in Tientsin. In Tientsin he was engaged in
the fur business and later worked as a pianist at
various hotels and cabarets in that city. After
the occupation of Tientsin by the Japanese Forces,
the applicant was an active member of the Anti-
Communist Committee, for some time being a commander
of the Officers Company of Russian Volunteers.
In May 1939 he was arrested for some unknown
reason, and after being kept prisoner at the so-called
"White House" for about 30 days, was subsequently
deported to Shanghai, arriving at this port in the
beginning of June, 1939. Here he again worked in
his professional capacity as a pianist until September,
since which he has been unemployed.

2. Dmitry Dmitrievitch KIREEVSKY, Russian,
was born on October 21, 1919 at Blagoveschensk,
Maritime Province, Russia. He left Russia together
with his parents in 1920 and subsequently resided
in Harbin, Manchuria. He arrived in Shanghai from
Harbin on November 17, 1939 and is not known locally.

Subject V.V. Velissoff, N.P. Shoolgin, B.M. Mousalevsky and V.M. Mazavtzeff,
applicants for enlistment in the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.

Made by D. S. Pavloff. Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

1. Victor Vassilevitch VELISSOFF, Russian, was born on October 10, 1921 in Harbin, Manchuria. In 1923 he left Harbin for Tientsin together with his parents. In 1929 he entered the St. Loui's College on that city, graduating from same in 1935. In December 1938 he proceeded to Swatow where he resided together with his aunt Mrs. H. Ellis, wife of Mr. H. Ellis of the Chinese Maritime Customs. On September 29, 1939 the applicant arrived in Shanghai together with his aunt and resided at 118/1 Route de Souers, Apartment 3.

2. Nicolai Pavlovitch SHOOLGIN, Russian, was born on November 19, 1921 at Pogranichnaya Station, Chinese Eastern Railway. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on December 10, 1939 and is not known locally.

3. Boris Mihailovitch MOUSALEVSKY, Russian, was born on October 14, 1906 in Harbin, Manchuria. He arrived in Shanghai in January 1930 and in June of the same year obtained employment as a clerk with the Tkachenko Restaurant, Avenue Joffre. In March 1933 he left that place of employment of his own accord and on May 1, 1939 joined the Russian Auxiliary Detachment of the French Police. On June 4, 1934 he left the Detachment of his own accord and on June 15, 1934 was engaged as a ticket inspector by the China General Omnibus Co. He was employed in that capacity until December 11, 1939, when he resigned in order to join the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.

（左侧手写批注：Copy to Major Graham S.V.C.）
（左侧印章及手写字：FILE C 9/19.）

由 D. S. Pavloff 撰写。由 D. I. Crawford 转呈。

1. Victor Vassilevitch VELISSOFF，俄国人，1921年10月10日出生于满洲哈尔滨。1923年随父母离开哈尔滨前往天津。1929年进入该市圣路易学院（St. Loui's College），并于1935年毕业。1938年12月前往汕头，与其姨母 H. Ellis 夫人同住，后者系中国海关税务司 H. Ellis 先生之妻。1939年9月29日，申请人随其姨母抵达上海，居住于苏厄德路（Route de Souers）118/1号3室。

2. Nicolai Pavlovitch SHOOLGIN，俄国人，1921年11月19日出生于中东铁路边境站（Pogranichnaya Station）。他于1939年12月10日从哈尔滨抵达上海，本地无人知其底细。

3. Boris Mihailovitch MOUSALEVSKY，俄国人，1906年10月14日出生于满洲哈尔滨。他于1930年1月抵达上海，同年6月在霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）的 Tkachenko 餐厅受雇为职员。1933年3月他自行离职，并于1939年5月1日加入法国警察俄国辅助分队。1934年6月4日他自行离开该分队，并于1934年6月15日被英商中国公共汽车公司（China General Omnibus Co.）聘为查票员。他一直担任此职直至1939年12月11日，随后辞职以加入上海公共租界工部局义勇军俄国团。

（左侧手写批注：抄送上海公共租界工部局义勇军 Graham 少校。）

Lev Nicolaevich Primortsev/,father of Pavel levish Primortsev Trans-
baikal cossack arrived in China in 1921-2 with remnants of White Army.
It is known that he resided at Hailar,Manchuria near Mongolia from 1921-29
it is said that he had doubtful reputation and was strongly suspected in
horse stealing.

Later he resided with his family consisting of the wife E.A.Primor-
tseva nee Petigova(illiterate),son P.L.Primortseff(mentioned in attached
Question List if RED),daughter E.L.Primortseff born on 21 April 1921 and
son Alexey Lvovich Primortsev( subject of BIF File D.917/348 born on
25.VIII.1921 at Hailar,son Fedor Lvovich Primortsev ,born on 27 April 1925

From 1921 to 1929 he resided at Hailar.
" 1929 to 1935 at Harbin.
" 1935 - 1936 at Peiking.
" 1936 - 1937 Tsinanfu.
" 1937 to 1946(?) at Shanghai.

It is known that before his departure from Shanghai he owned a small
bar 96 Rue Grouchy together with his son Pavel Lvovich Primortsev.

According to SIF File D 917/345 Mrs E.A.Primortseva and her young
son Fedor were members of Repatriation Union already in 1939. Nothing is
mentioned re Pavel Lvovich Primortsev in this report !

Primortsev's family father mother ,P.L.Primortsev with his wife Helena
(Yelena) Primortseff and some other members were repatriated to USSR in 1946-7

In 1949 it was discovered by different Intelligences that Pavel Lvov-
ich Primortsev and his wife returned back to Shanghai. He was questioned by
the members of Chinese Intelligence including one Hassan Lin Deputy of the
Chief of Investigation Office of Ministry of Interior.F.L.Lojnikoff stated
that he was sent together with other former Russian emigrants repatriated
to USSR first to Port Nahodka near Vladivostok. Later he was residing
in Sverdlovsk Area, Ural.He was seen disappointed

1951年7月30日
列夫·尼古拉耶维奇·普里莫尔采夫（Lev Nicolaevich Primortsev），帕维尔·列维什·普里莫尔采夫之父，外贝加尔哥萨克，于1921-2年间随白军残部抵达中国。
已知他于1921-29年间居住在靠近蒙古的满洲海拉尔。
据说他声誉不佳，并被强烈怀疑从事盗马活动。

后来他与家人同住，家庭成员包括妻子 E.A. Primortseva（娘家姓 Petigova，文盲），儿子 P.L. Primortseff（在附带的红色问题清单中提及），女儿 E.L. Primortseff（生于1921年4月21日）以及儿子阿列克谢·利沃维奇·普里莫尔采夫（BIF 档案 D.917/348 的对象，1921年8月25日生于海拉尔），儿子费多尔·利沃维奇·普里莫尔采夫（生于1925年4月27日）

1921年至1929年居住于海拉尔。
" 1929年至1935年居住于哈尔滨。
" 1935 - 1936年居住于北平。
" 1936 - 1937年居住于济南府。
" 1937年至1946年(?)居住于上海。

已知在离开上海之前，他与儿子帕维尔·利沃维奇·普里莫尔采夫共同拥有一家位于格鲁西路96号的小酒吧。

根据 SIF 档案 D 917/345，E.A. Primortseva 夫人及其幼子费多尔早在1939年就是归国联盟的成员。本报告中未提及帕维尔·利沃维奇·普里莫尔采夫！

普里莫尔采夫一家——父亲、母亲、P.L. Primortsev 及其妻子海伦娜（叶莲娜）·普里莫尔采娃以及其他一些成员——于1946-7年被遣返回苏联。

1949年，各情报机构发现帕维尔·利沃维奇·普里莫尔采夫及其妻子返回上海。他受到中国情报人员的讯问，其中包括内政部调查局局长副手 Hassan Lin。F.L. Lojnikoff 称，他与其他被遣返回苏联的前俄罗斯侨民一起，首先被送往符拉迪沃斯托克附近的纳霍德卡港。后来他居住在乌拉尔的斯维尔德洛夫斯克地区。有人看到他感到失望

pages.en:
-2-

soon after his arrival in condition in U.S.S.R by bribing a doctor he was exempt
from labour as suffering from T.B.

Once pretending to go on hunting trip he boarded a train at other sta-
tion and left to Far East. At Irkutsk he succeeded to bribe a number of Control
Guard which check all passenger going in both direction and proceeded to
Amur Region.

He crossed according to him Amur river with his wife and left to
Harbin travelling from one town to the other. He was in possession of USSR
passport and besides has very good knowledge of Chinese language.

After staying for a period at Harbin P.L.Primortseff and his wife
left to Kirin(?) where they were detained by Intelligence Service of Chinese
Nationalist Government. Probably at that time they were questioned by USA
officers attached to Chinese Army.

Some time later P.L.Primortsev arrived to Shanghai. At Shanghai he was
very reserved regarding his adventures in USSR and refused to give informat-
ion to "Sino Chinese Newspaper" Kuomintang daily in Russian language. However
few articles describing his case with anti communist commentary appeared at
above daily. P.L.Primortsev objected, stating that he like to be out of poli-
tics. It should be mentioned that he was known as a member of Shanghai "under-
world" consisting of criminals, "Black Market operators and different shady
characters, many of them obtained USSR citizenship after termination of the
2nd Great War as "socially close" elements.

P.L.Primortsev maintained friendly relation with his former friends
and it seems returned only owing purely personal reason to Shanghai where
he had an "easy life" in his past.

It should be mentioned, that P.L.Primortsev from Sverdlovsk, Ural
sent to his aunt residing at Wayside District( MacGregor Rd ?) some of perso-
nal photos before he started his journey to Shanghai.
pages.zh:
-2-

抵达苏联后不久，他通过贿赂医生，以患有肺结核为由免除了劳动义务。

有一次，他假装去打猎，在另一个车站登上火车，前往远东。在伊尔库茨克，他成功贿赂了多名检查双向乘客的控制警卫，随后前往阿穆尔地区。

据他所说，他与妻子渡过阿穆尔河，离开前往哈尔滨，从一个城镇辗转至另一个城镇。他持有苏联护照，此外还精通中文。

在海拉尔停留一段时间后，P.L. Primortseff 和他的妻子离开前往吉林(?)，在那里他们被中国国民政府的情报部门拘留。可能在那时，他们受到了隶属于中国军队的美军军官的讯问。

一段时间后，P.L. Primortsev 抵达上海。在上海，他对自己在苏联的经历非常谨慎，并拒绝向国民党日报、俄文版的《中报》（Sino Chinese Newspaper）提供信息。然而，该日报刊登了几篇描述其案件并带有反共评论的文章。P.L. Primortsev 提出异议，称他希望远离政治。值得一提的是，他被认为是上海“ underworld ”（黑社会/底层社会）的一员，该群体由罪犯、“黑市”经营者和各种 shady characters（可疑人物）组成，其中许多人在第二次世界大战结束后作为“社会亲近”分子获得了苏联国籍。

P.L. Primortsev 与他以前的朋友保持友好关系，似乎纯粹出于个人原因返回上海，因为他过去在那里过着“轻松的生活”。

值得一提的是，P.L. Primortsev 在从乌拉尔斯维尔德洛夫斯克出发前往上海之前，曾将一些个人照片寄给居住在西区（麦格雷戈路？）的阿姨。

pages.en:
His wife Helene (Elena) Primakoff is a young, attractive, smart woman
It was strongly rumoured, that P.L.Primakoff invented all his story
and that he actually was at Peking or some other place in North China.
But Chinese authorities verified his statement and disclosed the fact, that
he corresponded with his aunt from USSR and sent abovementioned photos.
To escape from USSR is not easy and many were surprised, that he could
escape together with his wife. But it should be noted, that P.L.Primakoff
a member of "underground" who was close to Soviet and espionage circles at
Shanghai and his good knowledge of Chinese was just a type for this adventure;
pages.zh:
他的妻子海伦娜（叶莲娜）·普里马科夫是一位年轻、迷人、精明的女性。
有强烈的谣言称，P.L. Primakoff 编造了他的所有故事，实际上他当时在北平或华北的其他地方。
但中国当局核实了他的陈述，并揭露了他从苏联与阿姨通信并寄送上述照片的事实。
逃离苏联并非易事，许多人对他能与妻子一同逃脱感到惊讶。但值得注意的是，P.L. Primakoff 是“地下”成员，在上海与苏联及间谍圈子关系密切，而他良好的中文知识正是此类冒险活动的典型特征；

译文。
PRIMORTSEV 案

在第二区法院的亚历山德罗夫法庭审理了关于
向 P.L.Primortsev 追讨 1000 美元的案件，该款项是他从 P.M.Grinberg 处凭收据收取的。Primortsev 并不否认他收了钱，但向法院陈述说，
这笔钱是从 Lever 先生那里拿的。
原告律师 Grinberg 先生的法律顾问 P.Mishchki 出示了由
Primortsev 签署的收据，证明他从 Grinberg 处收款，并向法院解释说，
Lever 只是 Grinberg 先生企业的雇员。

随后法官询问被告能否在一个月内偿还债务，但 Primortsev 先生提议
每月支付 20 美元来清偿债务。

原告律师不同意，法官宣布上述案件的裁决将于
6月15日作出。

Made by. D. S. Pavloff. Forwarded by D. L. Crawford.

Kuzma Mefodiewitch KIBIREFF, Russian, was
born on October 12, 1920 in Transb-ikal Province,
Russia. According to his own statement, he escaped
from the U.S.S.R. together with his mother in 1929
and subsequently resided in Harbin. On November
15, 1939 he arrived in Shanghai from Harbin. On
21-11-39 he joined the Auxiliary Detachment, French
Police, however, on 23-11-39 he absented himself
without leave and was consequently discharged for
that reason.

Abdurahman GARIFOCLIN, Russian of Tartar
origin, was born on February 14, 1903 in Ufimsk
Province, Russia. He is reported to have left
Russia in 1922 and to have subsequently resided in
Mukden. From 1924 to 1927 he served in Marchall's
Chang Chung Chang Army and later again resided in
Mukden, where he worked as a chauffeur. In April
1929 he arrived in Shanghai and soon afterwards was
engaged as a chauffeur by the China General Omnibus
Company. He worked in that capacity until December
20, 1939 when he resigned on his own accord.

The above two applicants are registered with
the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records detrimental to their characters.

D. S. ( Special Branch ).

Subject V.N. Froloff and M.M. Tretiakoff - candidates for enlistment in the
Russian Regiment, S.V.C.

Made by. D.D.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by. W.L. Crawford.

1. Victor Nikolaevich FROLOFF, Russian, born
on June 7, 1921 at Pogranichnaya Station, Chinese Eastern
Railway. According to his own statement, he graduated
from a middle school at Harbin in 1934 and later studied
in the Y.M.C.A. College ( Commercial Section ) until
1940, after which he proceeded to Shanghai, arriving in
this city on 22-1-40 in the s.s. "Tsingtao Maru". Here
he resided with his sister who is married to Mr. Ivanoff-
Sumjieff, a corporal in the Russian Regiment, attached to
Headquarters as interpreter. Mrs. L.M. Tsicritsi, 616
Avenue Joffre, is applicant's aunt.

Froloff stated that his parents were divorced
some years ago at Harbin. His mother later married ano-
ther Russian and resides in Harbin at present, while his
father, Mr. N. Froloff, has been residing in Shanghai
for the past five or six years and at one time worked as
a teacher at the First Russian School, Kulin Road.

2. Mihail Nikiforovich TRETIAKOFF, Russian, born
on November 8, 1921 at Manchouli Station, Chinese Eastern
Railway. He arrived in Shanghai from Mukden in 1931 to-
gether with his parents. His father, a Transbaikal Cossack
died at Shanghai in 1936, and his mother, three sisters
and two brothers reside at 13 Rue Gaston Kahn. Mrs
Tretiakoff has been casually working as a char-woman etc.

In Shanghai the applicant attended St. Andrew's
elementary school for a short period, after which he
studied in the Russian Orthodox Confraternity's School,
Avenue Petain, and lived at St. Tichon's Orphanage.

（左侧手写批注：Copy sent to Major Graham SVC）

1. 维克托·尼古拉耶维奇·弗罗洛夫（Victor Nikolaevich FROLOFF），俄国人，1921年6月7日出生于中东铁路边境站（Pogranichnaya Station）。据其自述，他于1934年毕业于哈尔滨的一所中学，随后在青年会学院（商业科）就读至1940年，之后前往上海，于1940年1月22日乘“青岛丸”号轮船抵达本市。在此他与姐姐同住，其姐夫为伊万诺夫-苏姆吉耶夫先生（Mr. Ivanoff-Sumjieff），系俄国兵团下士，借调至总部担任翻译。申请人之姨母为 L.M. Tsicritsi 女士，住址为霞飞路616号。

弗罗洛夫称，其父母数年前在哈尔滨离婚。其母后嫁给另一名俄国人，目前居住在哈尔滨；其父 N. Froloff 先生过去五六年一直居住在上海，并曾在库林路第一俄侨学校担任教师。

2. 米哈伊尔·尼基福罗维奇·特里亚科夫（Mihail Nikiforovich TRETIAKOFF），俄国人，1921年11月8日出生于中东铁路满洲里站。他于1931年随父母从沈阳抵达上海。其父系外贝加尔哥萨克，于1936年在上海去世；其母、三个姐妹和两个兄弟现居住于加斯顿·坎恩路13号。特里亚科夫夫人曾零星从事清洁女工等工作。

在上海，申请人曾短暂就读于圣安德鲁小学，随后在贝当路俄罗斯东正教兄弟会学校学习，并居住在圣吉洪孤儿院。

S. V. C.
Made by. D. J. Pavloff Forwarded by. D. I. Crawford

Vladimir Ivanovitch TEREFF, Russian, was
born on July 28, 1909 in Omsk, Siberia. He is
reported to have left Russia together with his
parents in 1919 and to have subsequently resided
in Harbin. He first came to Shanghai in November,
1918 but after a short stay in this city returned
to Harbin in February, 1919. In Harbin he worked
for his father who is the owner of a small shop
dealing in furs and skins. It is also rumoured
that after the Japanese occupation of Manchuria
and until his departure to Shanghai in August,
1938, the applicant was employed as an agent by the
Japanese Gendarmerie in Harbin.

The applicant returned to Shanghai in the
s.s. "Dairen Maru" on August 3, 1938 and took
up residence at 72, Route Ferguson, where he is
still living.

On October 1, 1938 he joined the Russian
Regiment, S.V.C. in which he served until January
31, 1940, when he resigned of his own accord.
Since then he has been connected with the Ayurvedic
Hall, 651 Weihaivei Road, where he is employed as
an expert in electro therapy treatment.

While in Harbin, the applicant became a
naturalized Chinese citizen. In September, 1938
in Shanghai he renounced his allegiance to the
Chinese Government and registered with the Council
