I. Victor Dmitrievitch KOVIKIN , Russian, was
born on February 2, 1909 in Transbaikal Province,
Siberia. He arrived in Harbin from Vladivostok in
1919 and resided there until his departure to Shanghai.
Upon leaving school he casually worked in that city
until 1932 when he was engaged by I.I. Tchunin & Co.,
as a shop assistant. Leaving that firm of his own
accord in 1936 he proceeded to Sui-Hua City where he
was employed as a railway guard. He arrived in
Shanghai from Harbin in October 1938 and on November
18, 1938 joined the Russian Regiment, S.V.C. On
December 12, 1939 he left the Regiment of his own
accord and on January 7, 1940 proceeded to Harbin in
order to marry. On returning to Shanghai on February
1, 1940, he rejoined the Regiment and again resigned
on February 25th.

2. Peter Ivanovitch LEJNIN, Russian, was
born on September 13, 1910 in Voronej, Russia. During
the same year he arrived in Harbin, where his father
was employed with the Chinese Eastern Railway. He
arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on January 27, 1940
and took up residence at 197 Route Winling. His
brother, A. Lejenin, has been a member of the Russian
Regiment, S.V.C. since July 1, 1936.

3. Nikolai Kirillovitch ZORENKO, Russian, was
born on January 1, 1922 at Imianpo Station, Chinese

1. Alexander Nikolaevitch SOORINOFF,
Russian, was born on August 20, 1919 in Kazan
Province, Russia. According to his own statement,
he escaped from the U.S.S.R. together with his
mother in 1926 and subsequently resided in Harbin.
He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on February
10, 1940 and is not known locally.

2. Vladimir Mihailovitch SOCOLOFF, Russian,
was born on February 22, 1922 in Shanghai. From
1935 to December 1939 he studied in the St.
Joan D'Arc College. His father is employed as
a stoker with the Shanghai Power Company.

3. Mihail Artemievitch OSIPOFF, Russian,
was born on August 12, 1911 in Harbin, Manchuria.
For the past ten years he has been employed as an
assistant shop manager with Vorontzoff Brothers,
a well known firm in Harbin. On February 7,
1940 he arrived in Shanghai from Harbin and took
up residence together with his God mother, Mrs.
A.A. Krichevtzova at 510 Route Vallon.

The above three applicants are registered
with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1
Poulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records detrimental to their characters.

Manchuria. He arrived in Shanghai from Harbin on

Region, Siberia. He is reported to have left Russia
together with his parents in 1919 and to have subsequent-
ly resided in Harbin. He arrived in Shanghai from
Harbin on December 1, 1939 and is not known locally.

Forgy Alexeyevich SOKOLOFF, Russian, born on
13-5-1906 at Blagoveschensk, Amur Province, Siberia.
According to his own statement, he left Russia for China
1921 together with parents and for the following 13 years
resided in Harbin where he graduated from a Russian
Middle School in 1925 and later worked as a mechanic.
From 1934 to 1938 he resided at Tientsin. He holds a
testimonial from Frazer Automotive and Industrial Engi-
neers and Importers, to the effect that he was employed
by this firm for 5 years as a refrigerator and radio
mechanic. On behalf of this company he visited Nether-
lands East Indies in 1936, after which he arrived in
Shanghai.
Here he worked independently at his home as
a mechanic until November, 1938 when he secured his pre-
sent employment with Andersen Meyer Co., Ltd, at their
Yangtszepoo Works.
He is registered with the Russian Emigrants Com-
mittee, Route Poutreine Road, and with the French Police ( Re-
gistr. No. 9960 of 23-11-38 ).
At present he resides at 427 Avenue du Roi Al-
bert, Garage No 4.
There is nothing in the Municipal Police re-
cords detrimental to his character.

G. Prokofiev

Subject. I.K. Mrochkovsky, V.A. Willer, I.F. Lemann, V.N. Steher, F.I. Skopin and B.D. Dmitrieff - applicants for enrolment in the "C" (W.G.) Coy, S.V.C.
Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by Supt. J. Mason

FILE

1. Ivan Konstantinovich MROCHKOVSKY, Russian, born 28-3-1896 at Nijny-Novgorod, Russia. A graduate of the Military Cadets School in that city (1914) and of the Odessa School for Artillery Officers (1915) he served in the Russian army during the Great War from 1915 to 1918 and later fought against the bolsheviks in the ranks of the "White" army in Siberia from 1918 to 1922. He arrived in China from Vladivostok in November, 1922. In 1925 he joined the Russian Detachment of Marshal Chang Chung Chang's army in Shantung (Armoured Trains Division). In 1928 he was taken prisoner by the Nationalist army and later was engaged to serve in that army as an instructor. According to his own statement he was connected as an advisor with the 2nd Department of the General Staff of the Chinese Army, Nanking, until the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1937, after which he claims to have been working in Shanghai as a journalist. In Shanghai he has been generally known as an agent of the Chinese military intelligence service.
At present he resides at 559 - D. Rue Lafayette.
2. Vladimir Andreyevich WILLER, Russian, born on 18-9-1892 at Moscow. Former officer of the Russian army from 1914 to

have resided at Harbin. Upon graduating middle school in that city in 1927 he was employed with the Harbin branch of the National City Bank from 1927 to 1931

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特别分部登记处 编号 S. B. D. 917/362 日期 1940年3月8日。）
事由：I.K. Mrochkovsky、V.A. Willer、I.F. Lemann、V.N. Steher、F.I. Skopin 和 B.D. Dmitrieff —— 申请加入上海义勇队（S.V.C.）“C”连（W.G.）。
由副督察普罗科菲耶夫（Prokofiev）撰写，由警司 J. Mason 转呈

档案

1. 伊万·康斯坦丁诺维奇·姆罗奇科夫斯基（Ivan Konstantinovich MROCHKOVSKY），俄国人，1896年3月28日出生于俄罗斯下诺夫哥罗德（Nijny-Novgorod）。他毕业于该市的军事士官学校（1914年）和敖德萨炮兵军官学校（1915年），在第一次世界大战期间（1915年至1918年）服役于俄国军队，随后于1918年至1922年在西伯利亚的“白军”队伍中对抗布尔什维克。他于1922年11月从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达中国。1925年，他加入张宗昌元帅驻山东军队的俄国分队（装甲列车师）。1928年，他被国民革命军俘虏，随后受聘在该军中担任教官。据其自述，在1937年中日敌对行动爆发前，他一直以顾问身份隶属于南京中国陆军总参谋部第二厅，此后他声称在上海从事记者工作。在上海，他普遍被认为是中国军事情报机构的一名特工。
目前他居住在拉斐特路（Rue Lafayette）559-D号。

1. Ivan Konstantinovich MROCHKOVSKY, Russian, born
28-3-1896 at Nijny-Novgorod,Russia. A graduate of the Mi-
litary Cadets School in that city (1914) and of the Odessa
School for Artillery Officers (1915) he served in the Rus-
sian army during the Great War from 1915 to 1918 and later
fought against the bolsheviks in the ranks of the "White"
army in Siberia from 1918 to 1922. He arrived in China from
Vladivostok in November, 1922. In 1925 he joined the Russian
Detachment of Marshal Chang Chung Chang's army in Shantung
(Armoured Trains Division). In 1928 he was taken prisoner
by the Nationalist army and later was engaged to serve in
that army as an instructor. According to his own statement
he was connected as an advisor with the 2nd Department
of the General Staff of the Chinese Army,Nanking, until
the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1937,
after which he claims to have been working in Shanghai
as a journalist. In Shanghai he has been generally known
as an agent of the Chinese military intelligence service.
At present he resides at 559 - D. Rue Lafayette.

Vladivostok in November, 1922 together with the remainders
of the "White" army. From 1924 to 1927 he served in the Rus-
sian Detachment of Marshal Chang Chung Chang's army in
Shantung and from 1928 to the end of 1931 was employed
with the Netherlands Harbour Works Co., Hulutao. Arriv-

1. Sergey Sergeevich GRIGORIEFF, Russian, born
16-9-1899 in Simbirsk Province, Russia. In 1916 he gra-
duated from a middle school in Kazan after which he at-
tended the Petrograd Institute for Mining Engineers for
two years. Following the outbreak of the civil war in
Russia he served in the ranks of the "White" army in Si-
beria from 1918 to the end of 1922. In 1923 he arrived
in Shanghai from Vladivostok via Manchuria and shortly
afterwards left for Hongkong where he worked as a clerk
of works with an American firm from 1924 to 1927, Re-
turning to Shanghai he worked in the same capacity for
various periods with different local firms including
F.Berndt ( 1927 -1928 ), E.J. Muller ( 1929 -1930 ),
Leonard, Veysseryre & Kruze ( 1930 - 1932 ). From 1934
to 1935 he was employed in the Public Works Department,
S.M.C, after which he was connected with the Allied Con-
structing Co. from 1936 to 1938. For the following two
years he worked independently as a general contractor
and on 1-1-40 was re-engaged by E.J. Muller , Norwegian
Civil Engineers, 2 Peking Road, his present employers.
In 1934 -1938 he served in the 3rd (Vol.) Coy,
Russian Regiment, S.V.C.
He is one of the prominent members of the Rus-
sian Sporting Association "SOKOL", 888 Weihaiwei Road.
At present he resides at 1025 Bubbling Well Road
House 7, Room 4.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by Supt. J. Mason

1. Vladimir Alexeyevich BOUTSKOI, Russian, born on
7-5-1891 in Orel province, Russia. In 1910 he graduated
from the Naval Officers School at Petrograd and subse-
quently served in the Russian Navy until the outbreak of
the revolution in Russia in 1917. During the civil war
in Russia he served in the "White" army in South Russia
following the defeat of which he made his way to Mesopota-
mia where he was interned for a period. In 1922 he arrived
in Vladivostok. Towards the end of the same year he pro-
ceeded to Manila via Shanghai together with Admiral Stark's
flotilla. Returning to Shanghai from Manila in July, 1923
he has since been residing in this city. Since 1924 he has
been employed with Butterfield & Swire.
He resides at 27/2 Rue Paul Henry.

2. Konstantin Konstantinovich AKINTIEVSKY, Rus-
sian, born 14-10-1884 in Chernigov province, Russia. In
1905 he graduated from an Artillery Officers School at
Petrograd and in 1913 from the Petrograd Military Academy.
He saw active service in the Russian army during the Great
War and also participated in the civil war in Siberia un-
til 1920, after which he resided at Harbin for the follow-
ing 15 years. During this period he is known to have been
associated with the Monarchist movement amongst Russian
emigrants. In September, 1935 he arrived in Shanghai from
Harbin. It is reported that he and several other prominent
Russian emigrants were obliged to leave Manchuria because
their political convictions were disapproved by the Japanese
authorities.

1. 弗拉基米尔·阿列克谢耶维奇·布茨科伊（Vladimir Alexeyevich BOUTSKOI），俄国人，1891年5月7日出生于俄罗斯奥廖尔省。1910年毕业于彼得格勒海军军官学校，随后在俄罗斯海军服役，直至1917年俄罗斯革命爆发。在俄罗斯内战期间，他在南俄罗斯的“白军”中服役，战败后前往美索不达米亚，并在那里被拘禁了一段时间。1922年，他抵达符拉迪沃斯托克。同年年底，他随斯塔克（Stark）海军上将的舰队经上海前往马尼拉。1923年7月从马尼拉返回上海后，他一直居住在本市。自1924年以来，他一直受雇于宝顺洋行（Butterfield & Swire）。
他居住在亨利路（Rue Paul Henry）27/2号。

2. 康斯坦丁·康斯坦丁诺维奇·阿金季耶夫斯基（Konstantin Konstantinovich AKINTIEVSKY），俄国人，1884年10月14日出生于俄罗斯切尔尼戈夫省。1905年毕业于彼得格勒炮兵军官学校，1913年毕业于彼得格勒军事学院。他在第一次世界大战期间在俄军中服现役，并参加了西伯利亚的内战，直至1920年，此后他在哈尔滨居住了15年。在此期间，据悉他与俄罗斯侨民中的君主主义运动有关联。1935年9月，他从哈尔滨抵达上海。据报道，他和另外几位著名的俄罗斯侨民因政治信仰不为日本当局所容，被迫离开满洲。

1. Serafim Petrovitch PARITSKY, Russian, was
born on August 26, 1905 in Sedletz Province, Russia.
In 1922 he completed his course of study at the
Khabarovsk Cadet School after which he entered the
Military Officers' School at Vladivostok. Upon the
defeat of "whites" in Vladivostok he left for China
via Genzan, arriving in Shanghai in the autumn of 1923.
In December of the same year he left for Harbin for the
purpose of continuing his education. He remained in
that town until 1927 when he joined the Russian
Detachment under Marshal Chang Chung Chang and served
with this unit until the end of 1928 when Chang's
forces were disbanded. In November 1928 he returned
to Shanghai and soon afterwards obtained employment
with the Shanghai International Greyhounds Ltd. at the
Stadium race track, where he worked until the beginning
of 1931 when that company was closed down. During
the same year he proceeded to Macao where he was
engaged as an assistant dog trainer by the Hongkong and
Macao Sports Club. He worked in that capacity until
October 1936 when the company ceased functioning.
Returning to Shanghai during the same month he obtained
employment as a watchman with Anderson Meyer & Co., Ltd.,
He left that place of employment of his own accord in
March 1937. From 13-10-37 to 31-5-38 he served with
the Auxiliary Detachment of the French Police. Between
1-11-38 and 1-1-40 he worked as an Anti-Piracy Guard

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by Supt. J. Mason.

1. Vladimir Nikolaevich DUNAEFF, Russian, born
on January 9, 1897 at Warsaw. According to his own state-
ment, he left the U.S.S.R. for Manchuria early in 1931
and in March of the same year arrived in Shanghai. From
10-8-31 to 1-9-33 he was employed with Meyer Construction
Corporation, 24 The Bund, as a watchman and assistant su-
pervisor. For the following five years he casually work-
ed with various local firms including the Radio Doctor
Service, Ellers Construction Co and Graphic Printing Es-
tablishment. From 6-8-38 he has been employed as a watch-
man with Shanghai Inland Water Navigation Co., 434 N. Soo-
chow Road. Since 16-7-34 he has been on the S.M.P. list
of approved candidates for the position of a police watch-
man and/or bodyguard.
At present he resides at 569/1 Avenue du
Roi Albert.

2. Victor Vassilievich ORLOFF, Russian, born on
14-9-1913 in Pskov Province, Russia. He is reported to
have left Russia for Manchuria in 1919 and for the follow-
ing 13 years to have resided at Harbin. In November,
1933 he arrived in Shanghai from Dairen. Here he is known
to have worked as a musician ( violinist ) in various lo-
cal cabarets and night clubs. On several occasions he
was absent from Shanghai to Tsingtao, Chefoo etc. to work
there in the same capacity.
His last known address in Shanghai is 347
Avenue du Roi Albert, Apt. 2.

1. Vladimir Nikolaevich DUNAEFF，俄国人，1897年1月9日
出生于华沙。据其自称，他于1931年初离开苏联
前往满洲，同年3月抵达上海。从1931年8月10日至
1933年9月1日，他受雇于外滩24号的迈耶建筑公司，
担任看守兼助理监工。在接下来的五年里，他在包括
无线电医生服务社、埃勒斯建筑公司和图形印刷所在内的
多家本地公司零星工作。自1938年8月6日起，他受雇于
北苏州路434号的上海内河航运公司，担任看守。自
1934年7月16日起，他名列工部局警务处批准的警察
看守和/或保镖候选人名单。
目前他居住在阿尔伯特王路 569/1 号。

2. Victor Vassilievich ORLOFF，俄国人，1913年9月14日
出生于俄罗斯普斯科夫省。据报道，他于1919年离开
俄罗斯前往满洲，并在随后的13年里居住在哈尔滨。
1933年11月，他从大连抵达上海。在此间，据悉他在
本地多家歌舞厅和夜总会担任乐师（小提琴手）。他曾
数次离开上海前往青岛、烟台等地，以相同身份工作。
其在上海的最后一个已知地址是阿尔伯特王路 347 号，
2 室。

Date April 6, 1940 H.C
Subject M. Greenberg, applicant for enrolment in American Troop, S.V.C.
Made by D. S. Pavloff Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

Meyer Greenberg, Russian Jew, was born on
November 10, 1915, at Shanghai. His father, Mr.
B. Greenberg, owns a fur store at 978 - 980
Bubbling Well Road. Meyer Greenberg first came to
the notice of the Municipal Police in 1930 while
he was a school-boy attending the Public and Thomas
Hanbury School.

During July, 1930, complaints were made
to the Tsingtao Authorities concerning thefts
of money and jewellery from a bathing hut on the
beach which Greenberg was sharing and he was
strongly suspected of the thefts. On returning
to Shanghai from Tsingtao on July 28, 1930,
information was laid with the Municipal Police that
Greenberg was wearing the wrist watch which was
stolen in Tsingtao. Greenberg was not charged
on this occasion and the watch was returned to its
owner, but the money totalling $30.00 and the brooch
were not recovered.

Meyer Greenberg again came to the notice of
the Municipal Police in November, 1930 when he was
arrested with two young British subjects in
connection with the forging and uttering of a cheque
for $150.00. All three youths were charged and
Greenberg was subsequently arraigned for trial
before the 1st Shanghai Special District Court
and sentenced on November 27, 1930 to three months
imprisonment suspended for three years.

迈耶·格林伯格（Meyer Greenberg），俄籍犹太人，
1915年11月10日出生于上海。其父B. Greenberg先生
在静安寺路978-980号拥有一家皮草店。迈耶·格林伯格
首次引起警务处注意是在1930年，当时他是公和汉伯里学校
（Public and Thomas Hanbury School）的一名学生。

1930年7月期间，有人向青岛当局投诉，称在海滩上一间
由格林伯格共用的更衣棚内发生钱款和珠宝失窃案，
格林伯格有重大盗窃嫌疑。1930年7月28日从青岛返回
上海后，有人向警务处举报，称格林伯格佩戴着在青岛
被盗的手表。此次格林伯格未被起诉，手表也归还给了
失主，但总计30.00元的现金和一枚胸针未能追回。

迈耶·格林伯格再次引起警务处注意是在1930年11月，
当时他因涉及伪造并使用一张面值150.00元的支票，
与两名年轻的英国臣民一同被捕。这三名青年均被起诉，
格林伯格随后在上海第一特区地方法院受审，并于
1930年11月27日被判处监禁三个月，缓刑三年。

Enquiries at this time also revealed that Greenberg had acquired the habit of hiring public motor cars and signing false names to the motor car chits.
Greenberg is reported to have worked from February, 1932 to April, 1933 with the firm of Heath Importers and Exporters, Tea Merchants, 2 Peking Road. In July 1933 he obtained a position with Reiss Massey and Co. In Hongkong, it came to the notice of his employers that he had a record and he was later dismissed but before leaving the company in Hongkong, a typewriter was found to be missing and Greenberg was suspected of the theft, but no action was taken in the matter.
On August 10, 1933 he again visited Hongkong and after a short stay in that city returned to Shanghai in September of the same year.
In the beginning of 1934, he secured his present position as a general office assistant with S.E. Levy & Company, 113 Kiukiang Road.

Made by D. S. Pavloff. Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

（批：Copy sent to Staff Office）
（批：24/4）

1. Leonid Iosifovitch VASSILIEFF, Russian,
was born on May 28, 1920 in Blagoveschensk, Amur Region,
Russia. He arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostok in 1922
together with his parents. Until 1937 he studied in the
Commercial School of the Russian Orthodox Confraternity
and later in the First Russian School (now A. S. Poushkin
Memorial School), graduating from same in June 1939.
His sister is married to Captain Poronik
of the Russian Regiment, S. V. C.

2. Alexander Prohorovitch ROMANOFF, Russian,
was born on January 23, 1913 in Chita, Siberia. He is
reported to have left Russia together with his parents
in 1919 and to have subsequently resided in Manchouli
and later in Harbin. From 1933 to December 1938 he has
been employed with the Harbin Railway Police and later
worked as a chauffeur of a hire car. He arrived in
Shanghai from Harbin on February 21, 1940 and is not known
locally.

3. Ioann Georgievitch LAMBIRIS, Russian, was
born on October 13, 1920 in Mukden. In 1930 he proceeded
to Tientsin together with his mother. Until 1938 he
studied at the St. Louis College. Until his departure
to Shanghai he has been employed as a passport
Inspector with the Peking-Mukden Railway.

1. 列昂尼德·约瑟福维奇·瓦西里耶夫（Leonid Iosifovitch VASSILIEFF），俄罗斯人，
1920年5月28日出生于俄罗斯阿穆尔州布拉戈维申斯克。1922年，他与父母一同
从符拉迪沃斯托克抵达上海。直至1937年，他在俄罗斯东正教兄弟会商业学校就读，
随后在第一俄语学校（现为A. S. 普希金纪念学校）就读，并于1939年6月毕业。
他的姐姐嫁给了上海义勇队俄国团的波罗尼克（Poronik）上尉。

2. 亚历山大·普罗霍罗维奇·罗曼诺夫（Alexander Prohorovitch ROMANOFF），俄罗斯人，
1913年1月23日出生于西伯利亚赤塔。据报他于1919年与父母一同离开俄罗斯，
随后居住在满洲里，后迁居哈尔滨。1933年至1938年12月期间，他受雇于哈尔滨铁路警察，
后来担任出租车的司机。他于1940年2月21日从哈尔滨抵达上海，本地对其不了解。

3. 伊万·格奥尔基耶维奇·兰比里斯（Ioann Georgievitch LAMBIRIS），俄罗斯人，
1920年10月13日出生于沈阳。1930年，他与母亲一同前往天津。直至1938年，
他在圣路易斯学院（St. Louis College）就读。在前往上海之前，他一直受雇于
北宁铁路（Peking-Mukden Railway），担任护照检查员。
他于1940年3月21日从天津抵达上海。
由于是新来者，本地俄国社区对其不了解。

Sviatoslav Nikolaevitch BOGUNSKY, Russian,
was born on January 1, 1922 in Kiev Province,
Russia. According to his own statement he escaped
from the U.S.S.R. together with his mother in 1927
and subsequently resided in Harbin. In 1933 he
arrived in Shanghai from Harbin and in 1934 entered
the St. Francis Xavier's College in which he studied
until June, 1939.

His mother is employed as a housekeeper with
Mr. Valejanin, Grosvenor House, Route Cardinal
Mercier.

Leonid Sergeyevitch ZIVINSKY, Russian, was
born on February 6, 1922 in Pogranichnaya Station,
Manchuria. He later resided at various stations
along the Chinese Eastern Railway, as his father was
been employed with that concern until 1935.

On March 28, 1940 he arrived in Shanghai from
Harbin and is not known in the local Russian community.

The above two applicants are registered with
the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1. Moulmein
Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records detrimental to their characters.

born on July 26, 1915 in Vladivostok, Maritime Province,
Russia. In 1925 he arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostok.

together with his parents and returned here in October

1937 he worked as a Commercial Artist at the Studio
Department of Millington Ltd., 668 Szechuen Road. Later

business, Pacific Stamp Company, 973 Bubbling Well Road.
In November 1939 he secured his present
employment as an office assistant and draughtsman with
the United Mechanical Industries, 138 Kiangse Road.
This applicant is registered with the Russian

Ury Andreyevitch SDOBNIKOFF, Russian, was
born on July 21, 1915 at Barnaul, Siberia. According
to his own statement, he left Russia for China in 1925
together with his mother and after a short stay in
Harbin proceeded to Tientsin where he resided for the
following 14 years. In 1934 he graduated from the
St. Louis College in that city, after which he is
reported to have been employed as an office assistant
with the Oriental Trading & Engineering Corporation from
January 1935 to November 1937, when the firm was closed.
His next employment was with the Concordia, Societe Vin-
cule, as an accountant (March-November, 1938). Leaving
this company of his own accord he joined the American
Textile Co., where he worked in the same capacity from
November 1938 to May 1939. From May 1939 to August
1939 he worked in the Transport Department of Siemssen
& Company, after which he left for Shanghai, arriving
in this city on September 3, 1939.

While in the employ of the Oriental Trading
& Engineering Company, he was attached to the Shanghai
Branch of this firm for about one year, 1936-1937.

On September 25, 1939 he secured his present
position with the Accountant Department of Moller Ltd.,
30 Foochow Road.

This applicant is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

Evgeny Ivanevitch BRAYNER, Russian, was
born on January 27, 1914 in Petrograd, Russia. He
is reported to have left Russia together with his
parents in 1920 and to have subsequently resided in
Harbin. On July 9, 1931 he arrived in Shanghai
from Harbin and has since been residing in this
city. While here, he has been employed at the
following places :- 1932 to 1933 as a mechanic
with the Bills Motors, Fed. Inc. U.S.A.; 1933-34
as an electrician with Messrs Arc Welders, 781
Wuting Road; 1935 - September 1936 as a mechanic
and electrician with Moller's Ltd.; 1936 -
December 1938, as a shop manager with Bata Shoe
Company. In January 1939 he obtained his
present position as a masseur with Kortus Orthopedic
Institute, 679 Szechuen Road. The applicant is
in possession of good references from his former
employers.
There is nothing in the Municipal Police records
detrimental to his character.

D. S. Pavloff

Maritime Province, Russia. In 1924 he arrived in
Shanghai from Vladivostok together with his parents.

District Court on September 7, 1937, and was
sentenced to 3 months imprisonment, suspended for
two years.

Subject E.I. Kukushko, applicant for enlistment in the Russian
Regiment, S.V.C.

Made by D.S. Pavloff Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

Evgeny Ivanovitch KUKUSHKO, Russian, was
born on March 27, 1908 in Ekaterinoslav Province,
Russia. In 1910 he proceeded to Harbin together
with his family, where his father was employed
with the Chinese Eastern Railway. In 1927 he
graduated from the Harbin Commercial School and
in 1930 proceeded to U.S.S.R. According to his
own statement he escaped from the U.S.S.R. and
returned to Harbin in 1933 and upon his return
took out emigrants papers through the Bureau for
the Affairs of Russian Emigrants in Manchoukuo.
The applicants father who was a Soviet citizen left
Harbin for the U.S.S.R. in 1935, after the sale
of the Chinese Eastern Railway to the Japanese.
The applicant arrived in Shanghai together
with his mother on May 20, 1940 and is not known
locally.
He is registered with the Russian Emigrants'
Committee, 113/1 Moukmeir Road.
There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records detrimental to his character.

Subject. V.H. Golbraih applicant for enlistment in the Transport Coy., S.V.C.

Made by. D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by Supt. J. Mason.

Vulf Haimovich GOLBRAIH, Soviet citizen of Jewish origin, was born on December 27, 1914 at Manchouli, Manchuria. According to his own statement, he left the U.S.S.R. for China in 1922 together with his parents and for the following 16 years resided in Tientsin where he attended the St. Louis College for five years. Leaving the college in 1928 he worked in a local garage as an apprentice for three years. Later he was employed as a chauffeur-mechanic in Mark Ferber's Hire Garage (1936) and with Mr. J.B. Affleck, British Consul-General at Tientsin, for about 7 months (1938). He holds a good testimonial from Mr. E.G. Jameson who succeeded Mr. Affleck on the post of Consul-General.

Applicant arrived in Shanghai from Tientsin some time in September, 1938. Here he was employed as a chauffeur with various local firms including James Neil & Co, Steinberg's Transportation Service Co, Chevrolet Transport Co and Union Brewery Co. until September, 1939 when he secured his present position as a fitter in the China General Omnibus Co.

He resided at various addresses in the French Concession until April, 1940 when he moved to 35 Aungping Road together with his mother. According to him, his father, Haim Golbraih, a commission agent by occupation, is also in Shanghai, but on account of bad relations between them he even does not know his father's address. His younger brother is employed with the Bakerite Bakery.

Applicant holds Soviet passport No. 76915 issued on

Vulf Haimovich GOLBRAIH，犹太裔苏联公民，
于 1914 年 12 月 27 日出生于满洲里，满洲。
据其自述，他于 1922 年随父母离开苏联前往中国，
并在随后的 16 年里居住在天津，期间在圣路易斯学院
就读五年。1928 年离校后，他在当地一家汽车修理厂
当了三年学徒。后来，他在马克·费伯租赁车行
（Mark Ferber's Hire Garage，1936 年）以及英国驻天津
总领事 J.B. Affleck 先生处（1938 年，约 7 个月）
担任司机兼机械师。他持有继 Affleck 先生之后
担任总领事的 E.G. Jameson 先生出具的良好推荐信。

申请人于 1938 年 9 月某时从天津抵达上海。
在此，他受雇于多家本地公司担任司机，包括

Valentin Dmitrievitch ROGOFF, Russian,
was born on October 2, 1903 in Samara, Russia.
In 1922, he arrived in Shanghai from Vladivostok.
In Shanghai he was employed as a Riding Instructor
in various Riding Schools until 1930, when he,
together with another Russian, named Krikoriants,
established a Riding Academy of their own, under
the name of Columbia Riding Academy. In 1937,
he sold his share in this business and proceeded
to Tsingtao, where, owing to his poor health,
he resided until the end of 1939, after which
he returned to Shanghai. Since his return he
has been employed as manager of the Ascot Riding
Academy, 200 Tunsin Road.

The applicant left Shanghai for
Tsingtao on June 30, 1940 and is expected to
come back in two months time.

He is registered with the Russian
Emigrants' Committee, 118/1 Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal
Police records detrimental to his character.

Subject E.A. Vedeniaeff and V.I. Petroff, applicants for enlistment
in the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.

Made by D. S. Pavloff. Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

Evgeny Alexandrovitch VEDENIAEFF, Russian,
was born on November 12, 1917 in Moscow, Russia.
He is reported to have left Russia together with
his parents in 1919 and to have subsequently
resided in Harbin. In August 1931 he arrived
in Shanghai from Harbin and at the beginning of
1932 entered the Commercial School of the Russian
Orthodox Confraternity, in which he studied up to
1936.

He failed to find any fixed employment
and was supported by his sister, Baroness R. D'Anxon
de Ruffe, 56 Rue Massenet.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records detrimental to his character.

Vassily Ignatievitch PETROFF, Russian,
was born on March 1, 1922 in Harbin, Manchuria.
In 1928 he left Harbin for Tientsin together with
his family and in 1931 arrived in Shanghai from
the latter city. Here for a period of one year,
1934-1935, he attended the First Russian High
School. Later he worked for short periods as
an apprentice and as a messenger at various shops
in the Concession but mostly he remained unemployed.

His elder brother is at present serving
with the Rusian Auxiliary Detachment of the French
Police.

Subject... V. P. Nikolaeff—applicant for enlistment in the Russian Regiment.
S.V.C.
Made by... D. S. Pavloff....................Forwarded by:...... D. I. Crawford.

Vladimir Pavlovitch NIKOLAEFF, Russian, was born on July 28, 1922 in Habarovsk, Maritime Province, Russia. In the previous year his mother, Miss. V. Nikolaeff, became the common law wife of one P. Egalevitch, but the applicant has always been known under his mother's maiden name. The applicant is reported to have left Russia, together with his mother his mother in 1925 and to have subsequently resided in Harbin. In 1930 he arrived in Shanghai from Harbin together with his mother and grand-father, Colonel N.N. Nikolaeff, Leader of the Russian Monarchist Legitimists in Shanghai.

During 1930 and 1931 the applicant attended the Commercial School of the Russian Orthodox Confraternity. In 1933 he proceeded to Tsingtao and resided there until 1937 during which period he studied in the Tsingtao American School. It is reported that during that time, his mother was either married to or cohabited with one Horton, American, Chief Petty Officer of the U.S.S. Canopus, and that in Tsingtao the applicant was known under the name of Horton.

The applicant returned to Shanghai in 1937 and in December 1938 entered the St. Francis Xavier's College, where he studied until July 1939, since which date he has been without any fixed employment.

Vladimir Pavlovitch NIKOLAEFF，俄国人，1922年7月28日出生于俄罗斯滨海省哈巴罗夫斯克。前一年，其母 V. Nikolaeff 小姐成为 P. Egalevitch 的事实婚姻妻子，但申请人一直以其母婚前姓氏为人所知。据报，申请人于1925年随其母离开俄罗斯，随后居住在哈尔滨。1930年，他随母亲及祖父 N.N. Nikolaeff 上校从哈尔滨抵达上海，其祖父是上海俄罗斯君主正统派领袖。

1930年和1931年期间，申请人就读于俄罗斯东正教兄弟会商业学校。1933年，他前往青岛并居住至1937年，在此期间就读于青岛美国学校。据报，在此期间，其母与美国军舰“卡诺普斯”号（U.S.S. Canopus）的士官长、美国人 Horton 结婚或同居，且申请人在青岛时以 Horton 为名。

Subject S. L. GREY, applicant for enrolment in American Troop, S.V.C.

Made by D. S. Pavloff Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

Semen Leonidovitch GREY, Russian, was born on
July 22, 1912 in Harbin, Manchuria. He graduated
from a Harbin high school in 1928 and subsequently
proceeded to Shanghai, arriving in this port in
August 1928. Here he resided unemployed, together
with his mother until 1930 after which he took
up work as a salesman with various local firms
dealing in motor cars.

During the summers of 1934-35-and 36 he
operated a shooting gallery in Chefoo and during
the winters of the same years was employed as a
physical instructor with the now defunct Knije's Phy-
sical Institute, corner of Seymour and Weihaiwei
Roads.

From 1936 he has been a representative of
the Gold and White Label, State Whisky and since
December 1939 has had a half share in the Dixie
Bar, 544 Avenue Joffre, at which address he at
present resides.

This applicant is not registered with the
Russian Emigrants' Committee or any other Russian
Public Organisation.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records detrimental to his character.

D. C. (Special Branch)

L. C. Pavloff
D. S.

Semen Leonidovitch GREY，俄国人，1912年7月22日出生于满洲哈尔滨。1928年毕业于哈尔滨一所高中，随后前往上海，于1928年8月抵达该港口。在此地，他与母亲一起失业居住，直至1930年，之后他在多家当地汽车经销公司担任销售员。

在1934、1935和1936年的夏季，他在烟台经营一家射击场；在同几年的冬季，他受雇于现已倒闭的 Knije 体育研究所（位于西摩路与威海卫路转角）担任体育教练。

自1936年起，他一直是金标和白标国家威士忌（Gold and White Label, State Whisky）的代表，自1939年12月起，他拥有霞飞路544号 Dixie 酒吧的一半股份，目前居住在该地址。

该申请人未在俄罗斯移民委员会或任何其他俄罗斯公共组织登记。

Made by D. S. Pavloff Forwarded by D. S. I. Logan

Valentin Ivanovitch SADOVSCHIKOFF, Russian,
was born on March 22, 1919 in Harbin, Manchuria.
He graduated from a Harbin high school in 1937
and subsequently continued his education in the
North-Manchurian University until 1940.

On August 7, 1940, he arrived in Shanghai
from Harbin and is not known locally.

Peter Petrovitch WELTZ, Russian, was born
on March 10, 1919 in Verhneudensk, Transbaikal
Province, Russia. He is reported to have left
Russia together with his parents in 1922 and
to have subsequently resided in Harbin.

On July 29, 1940, he arrived in Shanghai
from Harbin.

Being a new arrival here he is not known
in the local Russian Community.

The above two applicants are registered
with the Russian Emigrants' Committee, 118/1
Moulmein Road.

There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records detrimental to their characters.

Made by... D.Ss. Payloff Forwarded by: D.S.I. Logan

Samuel Solomonovitch SINGER, Russian Jew,
was born on February 19, 1911 in Harbin, Manchuria.
He arrived in Shanghai in November, 1926. In
1929 he obtained a position as a sales-man with
the now defunct Far Eastern Drug Trading Company.
He remained with that company until 1931 after
which he worked in the same capacity with the Claude
Neon Lights until February, 1932. He later worked
as a sales-man with the following firms in Shanghai :-
1932-34 with the American Engineering
Corporation
1934-36 with the Mustard and Company
1936-38 with the Union Brewery
In May, 1938 he obtained his present position
with the Ewo Brewery.
There is nothing in the Municipal Police
records detrimental to his character.
